name: Larkbourne Ford
unique_feature: a packhorse bridge over a bell that rings under the water when carts cross
story: The bridge was built over the Toll's fallen clapper; nobody could move it, so they paved around it. Carters say a crossing that rings twice means rain.
encounter: none by day; two bandits shake down late travellers after dark

name: Ansel's Hedge Shrine
unique_feature: a hawthorn grown through a stone chair, with a Hearthstone in its lap
story: Hearth-Mother Ansel sat here and told the first story about a neighbour. The hawthorn took the chair over the centuries; villagers still leave a pie on Naming Day.
encounter: none; a pilgrim NPC sometimes rests here

name: The Tumbled Watch
unique_feature: a Warden tower lying on its side down a dry valley, its stair now a corridor
story: It fell in the Quiet Villages years when its garrison stopped being talked about. Bandits use the lying stair as a hall; the Wardens want their old bell back from it.
encounter: skirmisher bandits in the stair-hall, a caster on the fallen parapet; approach from the hilltop to see them first

name: Gosling Pit
unique_feature: a chalk pit camp with a stolen mill wheel as a table
story: The Larkbourne Boys dug in below the Chalk Hound because nobody looks down when they can look up. The wheel came from Pennywort's Mill; the miller wants it back more than the thieves punished.
encounter: a pack of bandits with a brute leader; a rear path from the Hound's eye lets you drop in behind

name: The Singing Yew
unique_feature: a hollow yew with a small bell grown into its heartwood, humming in any wind
story: A Tamwick child hung a bell in a sapling; the tree ate it in three hundred years. Hedge-wights from the barrow will not pass it, which the orchard-keepers count on.
encounter: safe ground; a place to lure barrow-wights and watch them turn away

name: Whitecut Falls
unique_feature: the Larkbourne dropping off the chalk scarp in a single white sheet toward the Mere
story: The scarp is the edge the Toll cut when it fell. Down-wolves den in the spray caves behind the water.
encounter: a down-wolf pack in the cave behind the falls; wet stone slows dodges

name: Bell Meadow Stones
unique_feature: three leaning bronze-streaked stones where pieces of the Toll's crown landed
story: Each stone bears part of an Oroth word. The Sayers read them one way, the Wardens another, and the sheep sleep against them because they are warm.
encounter: none; a survey point that reveals the map around the Toll

name: Foxglove Dell
unique_feature: a dry valley entirely purple with foxgloves around a hedge-witch's turf hut
story: The hedge-witch Tansy Cresswell grows what Merrowby pretends not to buy. Something has been digging up her yew berries at night.
encounter: bristlebacks rooting in the dell at dawn; a charger fight in a narrow valley with soft banks

name: The Long Stride
unique_feature: an Oroth causeway whose hinge-less lamp posts light one after another at dusk
story: The Builders laid it to reach their foundation stone; the guilds charge a toll on it and pretend they built it.
encounter: cutpurses work the toll queue; a bravo duels anyone who refuses to pay

name: Shingle Shrine
unique_feature: a Hearthstone built of lake pebbles, each one a name scratched by a traveller
story: Travellers coming down out of the heights add a pebble here before the shore road to the city. The Tallymen tried to charge for it once; the pebbles were found in the guildmaster's bed.

name: North Cliff Beacon
unique_feature: a ruined beacon whose fire-bowl is an upturned Oroth bell
story: Lit only when the lake serpent was last seen, forty years ago. Smugglers use it now to signal the Undercroft.
encounter: smugglers with a dropout Sayer casting Hush; the cliff stair is the only way up unless you climb the drainage

name: The Gullhithe Wreck
unique_feature: a fishing smack broken on the shingle with gulls nesting in its nets
story: The Lamp went dark one night; the boat found the shore the hard way. The keeper says she was asleep. The gulls disagree.
encounter: gutter drakes in the hull; a smuggler's cache under the keel

name: The Eelweir
unique_feature: a wicker weir across the Mere's western outflow with a walkway of eel traps
story: Reedfolk and Lakefolk share the weir by an agreement neither has read. Every autumn someone is pushed in.
encounter: leech-hounds come up the channel at night

name: The Pilgrim Stair
unique_feature: Oroth steps that walk straight into the lake and keep going underwater
story: Nobody has counted the steps below the waterline and come back to say. A Sayer left a rope tied to the last dry one; it is still taut.
encounter: none above water; the sunken barge lies at the stair's foot

name: Willow Isle
unique_feature: an islet under a single pollarded willow the size of a barn, with a hermit's boat moored in its roots
story: The hermit Ivo Goslin was a Tallymen clerk who stopped counting. He will tell you the price of anything, correctly, and refuse to sell it.
encounter: none; a book and a side quest

name: The Bell Buoys
unique_feature: a line of twelve buoys whose bells ring in any wind, each tuned to a note of the Toll
story: The Sayers tuned them to prove the Bell account; on still nights they still ring, which proves nothing to anyone's satisfaction.
encounter: none; row out to hear the chord

name: The Lantern Causeway
unique_feature: a boardwalk of lantern poles lit each dusk by a lamplighter who sings as she goes
story: The lamplighter Lissane has walked it for forty years. When she is late the boardwalk is not safe, and she is late on purpose when she wants Isseva to notice her.
encounter: bog-drowned climb the poles after dark if the lanterns are out

name: Drowned Bell Shrine
unique_feature: a Hearthstone on a peat island above a bell that tolls once at midnight from under the water
story: The reedfolk bury their dead with lanterns; the bell is older than any of them and nobody buried it.

name: The Sallow King
unique_feature: a willow so old its branches have rooted again in a ring, making a hall of trunks
story: Sallowjaws nest under its roots and the reedfolk feed them so they nest nowhere else. It is the only place in the marsh where you are asked not to kill anything.
encounter: sallowjaw ambush from the water inside the ring; a moral choice with reputation cost

name: The Reed Wreck
unique_feature: a Salt Isles trading ship stranded three miles inland among the reeds
story: No flood on record could have carried it here. The reedfolk say the Tide came in once, briefly, and went out again; the ship's log stops the day before.
encounter: leech-hounds in the hold; a chart of the Salt Isles

name: The Stair of Isse
unique_feature: a sunken Oroth colonnade rising step by step out of the water toward the Drowned Nave
story: The Builders' processional way. The reedfolk call it Isse's Stair and say the Named woman walked down it into the water to teach the stilts.
encounter: bog-drowned rise from between the columns as you pass; fight on the steps, not in the water

name: Wisp Hollow
unique_feature: a dead-end channel where wisps gather over a drowned house whose chimney still stands
story: The family's lanterns were never lit for them; the wisps are what a water-burial becomes when nobody sings.
encounter: wisps lure toward deep water; silence them or ignore their light; a strongbox in the chimney

name: The Tideflat Stones
unique_feature: three stones on the sea's edge marking a shoreline that no longer exists
story: The soft western edge. Beyond them the flats go grey and the Salt Isles are a rumour. A survey point for the western chart.

name: Heron Watch
unique_feature: a reedfolk lookout on tall stilts with a bittern nesting in its bell
story: The watch was raised to see the Lakefolk coming for the weir. Now it is where young reedfolk go to be alone together.
encounter: none; a vista over the delta

name: Mossbridge
unique_feature: a natural granite arch over a ravine with a warden treant rooted at each end
story: The wardens let anyone cross who carries nothing they did not need. Poachers go round; it takes a day.
encounter: sentinels: do not fight them unless you are carrying stolen forest goods

name: The Oiled Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone the Woodfolk oil every week until it shines like a chestnut
story: Oiling is tending; tending keeps the note. The forester who forgets it is sent to the Briar for a month.

name: The Hunters' Stand
unique_feature: a high wooden hide built around a living trunk, reached by a rope ladder the poachers pull up
story: The poachers take hart and sell the antlers to Tollmere as Oroth relics. The Woodfolk have said nothing, which is the custom, and also a mistake.
encounter: skirmisher archers above; climb an adjacent tree to reach the platform level

name: Foxfire Falls
unique_feature: a fall into a ravine whose walls glow at night with foxfire fungus
story: The fungus is an alchemy ingredient worth a month's charcoal. Weavers string the ravine after dark.
encounter: weaver ambush from above at night; safe by day

name: The Hart Bones
unique_feature: an antlered skull the size of a house, of no beast anyone can name
story: The Hart-Knights wear antlers in its memory. The clans say it is a giant's dog. The Sayers say it is a mistake in the record.
encounter: a Hart-Knight keeps vigil at the skull; an elite duel with room to circle

name: The Breach
unique_feature: a gap in the Briar where the thorns have withered around broken Oroth wardstones
story: Something came through from the far side and the thorns died where it walked. Ash-wights, a long way from Cinderlea, wander near it. This is where the Briar's purpose becomes a question.
encounter: ash-wights (swarm) far from home; a main-quest clue

name: The Charcoal Camp
unique_feature: smoking turf kilns tended by burners who never sleep at the same time
story: The burners buy anything that burns and sell gossip that does not. A safe camp with a job board.

name: Fern Gully
unique_feature: a ravine so deep it holds mist at noon, crossed by silk bridges that hum
story: The back door to Weaverdeep. Woodfolk lost a whole hunting party here and left the bridges as a warning; the weavers kept them as a larder.
encounter: weavers on the bridges; cut a bridge to drop a pursuer; shortcut into Weaverdeep's lower level

name: The Chain Bridge
unique_feature: a bridge hung on four chains each forged by a different clan, across the gorge to Kharrow Hold
story: Each chain is a treaty. When a clan is shamed its chain is loosened one link, and the bridge leans.
encounter: a toll-keeper NPC; crag-wolves on the far approach at night

name: The Rib Cathedral
unique_feature: a giant's ribcage you walk through like a nave, each rib taller than a hall
story: The clans hold the Moot's oaths here because a giant's bones do not forget. Crag-wolves den in the skull at the far end.
encounter: crag-wolf pack in the skull; the ribs give cover from their knockdown charges

name: The Three Sisters
unique_feature: three terraced falls with a Hearthstone on the middle ledge behind the water
story: Three sisters of clan Rudd carried the Hearthstone up so their brother, exiled, could still be remembered somewhere warm.
encounter: none; scree-hags on the cliffs above shriek at climbers

name: The Clanless Camp
unique_feature: an overhang camp where exiled warriors have hung their loosened chain links as wind chimes
story: Every raider here was once someone's chain. They take from Brindlecrag's ore carts and claim it as their blood-price.
encounter: elite raiders in heavy plate; a brute and two skirmishers; approach along the ledge above the overhang

name: The Finger Shrine
unique_feature: a sinkhole whose central pillar is a giant's finger bone carved with memory-songs
story: The memory-keeper of clan Kharrow adds a line each year. The finger belongs to the Fallen Hand; nobody has explained how it got here.

name: The Watch of the Gate
unique_feature: the clan toll-house at Windgate, half buried in old snow, its bell frozen mid-swing
story: The soft northern edge. The gate-warden takes a toll for a pass nobody can cross until spring, and spring has not come in years.
encounter: none; the pass beyond is closed by avalanche

name: The Seven Stones
unique_feature: seven stones for seven clans, each grown over with a different colour of lichen
story: When a clan dies its stone loses its lichen within a year; there are seven stones and six clans, and the seventh is still green.
encounter: none; a survey point over the high moor

name: The Hidden Tarn
unique_feature: a high tarn behind a wall of scree, black and perfectly still, under the Cradle's mouth
story: The scree-hags fish it with their hands. Nothing lives in the water, and they still catch things.
encounter: scree-hags on the scree; ambushers and stone-throwers, silence their shrieks first

name: The Glass Bridge
unique_feature: a fused-stone Oroth bridge over a dry riverbed of black glass
story: The river was sung dry in the Ash Winter. The glass is the riverbed's last shape, and it is sharp.
encounter: ash-wights under the arch; the glass bed does bleed damage if you fight on it

name: The Pilgrims' Bell
unique_feature: a Hearthstone inside a fallen bell you enter through the crack in its side
story: The Order rings it once a day so the Choir knows it is still watched. Inside, the ringing goes on for an hour.

name: The Headless Watch
unique_feature: a colossus's fallen head hollowed into a watchtower, its eye the window
story: The Order keeps one knight in the eye at all times. The current one has been there eleven years and asks for news of Tollmere prices.
encounter: a fallen Tolling knight on the stair if the watch has turned; otherwise a friendly vigil

name: The One Poppy
unique_feature: a single red poppy in a square kilometre of grey grass
story: Nobody planted it and nothing eats it. Picking it is a deed the whole heath will know about by morning.
encounter: none; a Hollow deed if picked, a Hearth deed if watered

name: The Thirteenth
unique_feature: a thirteenth colossus lying face down far from the Choir's ring, as if it walked away
story: The Choir has twelve. This one has a head, buried in ash, and it is not the head of the others. A Sayer camp digs here and argues.
encounter: choristers around the excavation; casters whose note damages until silenced

name: The Cold Fire
unique_feature: ash-wights seated around a fire that went out a hundred and seventy years ago, still passing a cup
story: The people of Greyfold sat down to wait out the Ash Winter. They are still waiting, and they wave.
encounter: swarm; they only rise if you touch the cup

name: The Glass Falls
unique_feature: a dry waterfall of black glass, climbable, the shortcut up to the Choir plateau
story: Water still sounds here if you stand still. The Order forbids the climb and uses it themselves.
encounter: a bell-bearer at the top rings when it sees you; stun radius, break line of sight behind the glass ledges

name: The Hushline Stair
unique_feature: Oroth stairs descending into the mist where colour drains from your own hands
story: Where the Foundling walked out. Wren Tallow's Hearthstone at the top step is the first name you are given.
encounter: the tutorial: ash-wights on the stair; the mist turns you back below the fortieth step

name: The Stair Head
unique_feature: the Wardens' camp at the head of the Hushline Stair: a fire kept on the rim, grey-green colours on two poles, a lamp at the way out, and waystones walking north across the heath to the Choir
story: Where a new game hands over (DESIGN 5.1a). Wren Tallow keeps her fire here, above the Stair and out of the mist, and this is where she says the Foundling's name back. The position is the spot the Foundling stands on; the camp is laid out ahead of it, towards where its path leads.
encounter: none at the camp; the waystones keep more than fifty metres from anything the built world stands on the heath, and a test says which leg to move when a rebuild stands something nearer

name: The Wellspring
unique_feature: a Hearthstone set in the lip of the spring where the Larkbourne rises clear out of the end of the black glass bed, and sheep grazing the first green below it
story: Pilgrims going south fill a flask here and carry it to the line to pour out. The first clean water north of the ash, and the first Hearthstone a Foundling reaches in the living country.
hook: A pilgrim's flask comes back up the glass bed full, and the woman who filled it is written on the Chapter Roll as gone on.

name: Ash Watch
unique_feature: a Warden watchtower with a beacon fire-bowl kept laid, to be lit the night anything walks up the Glassbed
story: The Wardens raised a line of towers along the grey border after the Ash Winter; Ash Watch is the one nearest the Choir, and its keeper is changed every nine days so nobody grows used to the view.
hook: The beacon was lit last night and nobody on the Ash Watch roll admits to lighting it.

name: Hound Watch
unique_feature: a Warden tower on the south end of Hound Down with a bell hung in its crown to ring the alarm down the Vale
story: From Hound Watch the keeper can see the Choir's colossi, the piers at the head of the Stair and the whole length of the Vale, which is why the Wardens built it here and why its keepers drink.
hook: The keeper has started ringing the alarm at the colossi. He says they moved.

name: The Brow Beacon
unique_feature: the easternmost beacon of the Wardens' line, its fire-bowl on the highest chalk above the Hush
story: When the Brow Beacon burns, Rookdown shuts its doors and Bramcombe brings the flocks in. It was lit four times in a hundred years, and twice this spring.
hook: Lit twice this spring by a keeper who swears the Hush came up the cliff like a tide and went back down.

name: Orm's Long Barrow
unique_feature: a long barrow opened by robbers, its capstones stacked beside it like a dropped deck
story: Older than Hollin Barrow, whose first cist Orm Hollin dug. The robbers took nothing and stacked the stones neatly, which is what frightens the shepherds.
encounter: hedge-wights stand up among the stones at dusk
hook: The robbers left a roll in the cist older than the Wardens' own, and Tamwick is on it twice.

name: Hurdle Fold
unique_feature: a shepherds' summer camp inside a ring of woven hurdles, with a lambing lantern kept lit all night on a crook
story: Bram Down's shepherds live out here from lambing to shearing. The lantern on the crook is so the ewes know where the fold is in the dark.
encounter: down-wolves try the hurdles after dark
hook: The wolves have learned the lantern; the shepherds want somebody to sit the night with them and the crook.

name: Lamb's Bottom
unique_feature: a shepherd's stone hut in a dry valley that the down-wolves have taken for their den
story: The shepherd who built it walked south in the Quiet Villages years; the wolves moved in the winter after, and the Vale has let them keep it.
encounter: a down-wolf pack in the hut
hook: A bounty on the Lamb's Bottom pack, and in the hut a crook carved with a name the Roll struck.

name: The Last Field
unique_feature: a farmhouse left standing in a ploughed field that runs to the cliff edge, where the furrows go grey halfway down
story: The Southcotes ploughed this field to the Brow for three hundred years. The year the grey reached the middle furrow they left the plough in it and walked to Rookdown.
encounter: hedge-wights work the grey furrows at night
hook: The plough has moved a furrow since the Southcotes left it.

name: The Grey End
unique_feature: the southern end of the Briar, where the thorn runs down to the cliff and has gone grey to the root around a broken wardstone
story: Where the Thornmarch meets the Hush the thorn is dead and grey and does not fall down. Woodfolk come here to cut grey thorn for arrows that do not miss.
encounter: ash-wights wander up out of the Hush along the cliff after dark
hook: Both Briar pamphleteers want a grey thorn from the Grey End as evidence, for opposite reasons.

name: The Southgate Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone facing the Briar's south gate, where the Vale's carts went east when the gates still opened
story: One of the four Hearthstones the Briar's gates face. The wardstone over the gate reads HESK-THAEL VAEL; the Vale reads it as keep off and ties ribbons to it anyway.
hook: Someone has been leaving the south gate unbarred at night, from the inside.

name: Hanging Coombe
unique_feature: a bandit camp in a hollow of Rook Wood with stolen boundary-bells hung in the trees as a warning
story: The Larkbourne Boys' eastern gang steal the little bells the Vale hangs on boundary hawthorns, which is worse than it sounds: a boundary without its bell is a boundary nobody is keeping.
encounter: four bandits and the brute who leads them
hook: Take the boundary-bells back to their hedges; one of the hedges no longer bounds anything.

name: Hushwatch
unique_feature: three stones on the lip of the Brow set to frame the Hush, where the Vale comes to look at the grey and go home grateful
story: Vale families walk up on a clear evening to stand between the stones and look south. The custom is to say one name out loud before turning back.
hook: A child said a name between the stones that nobody in the Vale knows, and the name is on the Wardens' deep lines.

name: The Naming Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone where the downs' children are named on Naming Day, its face worn smooth by small hands
story: Every child born on the Brow is carried here in spring and named out loud to the stone, the shepherds and the sky. The stone keeps the names; the shepherds keep the party.
hook: The stone has a name worn into it that no child on the Brow was ever given.

name: The Flint Pits
unique_feature: a flint-diggers' camp among white spoil heaps, where the Vale's builders buy their flint by the cartload
story: The knappers dig shafts into the chalk and come up white to the eyebrows. They sell the Vale its walls and its sparks, and say the deepest shaft goes down into something that rings.
hook: The deepest shaft rings when struck; the knappers want a Sayer, a Warden or anyone braver than them to go down.

name: The Weighing Stone
unique_feature: a slab on three stones carrying a carters' weighing-beam, where the ridge road leaves the downs for the Wold
story: Dorrie Cooper weighs her hand-cart here going up and again at the top. The beam was set by the Tamwicks, who do not trust Woodfolk scales; the Woodfolk weigh again at the top.
hook: Dorrie's slate says the ridge road has eaten a cart and a half of goods in twenty years; the beam says it has not.

name: Wolf Holt
unique_feature: a sheepfold of flint walls on the downs' marsh edge that the down-wolves have taken back
story: Fallowfold's shepherds built it when the West Downs ran further west. The marsh came up and the wolves came with it.
encounter: a down-wolf pack in the fold
hook: The pack's leader wears a Warden's collar-bell, and the Wardens would like to know whose.

name: The Cress Bridge
unique_feature: a bridge of three chalk-white slabs on flint piers over the Cressbourne, with a coin wedged in every joint for luck
story: Carts to Tamwick cross here. The coins are Tamwick's toll to the water, paid in the Vale's way: nobody collects them, and nobody would dream of taking one.
hook: Somebody is taking the coins, one a night, and the Cressbourne has started to run low.

name: The Warden Barrow
unique_feature: the barrow of the first Wardens, its entrance kerb set with nine hand-bells that the youngest at the Rest rings on Tollday
story: The first Wardens were buried together on their own down so they could keep the Roll room in sight. Their bells are rung each Tollday by whoever is youngest at the Rest.
hook: The youngest at the Rest has stopped ringing the bells, because one of them rings back.

name: The Rod Stacks
unique_feature: a hazel-cutters' camp at the wood's edge with the season's rods stacked in wigwams to dry
story: Hazelcombe's cutters meet the Woodfolk here at the edge of the Wold to buy the rods. Neither side crosses the line of the stacks.
hook: The Woodfolk have stopped selling the Vale its rods, and the cutters want to know who in the Wold is saying no, and why.

name: The Sunk Plaza
unique_feature: a Builders' plaza sunk six steps into the ash, its fountain dry and full of little bells
story: Pilgrims drop a bell into the fountain on the way south, a habit older than the Order. The Order empties it into the chapter-house once a year and counts.
encounter: choristers sing in the plaza after dark
hook: The Order counts the fountain's bells every spring, and this year there is one more bell than there were pilgrims.

name: Bell Street
unique_feature: a street of the Builders' city lined with house-sized bells sunk to their shoulders in the ash
story: Each bell was a house, or a steeple, or both. Some are hollow and pilgrims shelter in them; one is not hollow, and hums.
encounter: ash-wights shelter in the hollow bells
hook: The bell that is not hollow: a Sayer wants it measured, the Order wants it left alone.

name: The Tower of Vaelost
unique_feature: an Oroth tower still standing over the Builders' city, its top course ringing faintly whenever wind crosses the heath
story: The tallest thing the Builders left in Cinderlea outside the Choir. The Sayers call it Vaelost, the kept one, and nobody has climbed it since its stair turned to glass.
encounter: a bell-bearer walks its round at the foot
hook: The top course has a name cut in it, and the Order will pay to know whose.

name: The Anthem Hall
unique_feature: a Builders' choir-school whose stone benches still face a singer who is not there
story: Anthe-Thael, the Sayers call it: the door of the choir. A whisper at the front is heard at the back as a shout, so pilgrims do not whisper in it.
hook: A lecture given here reaches the whole heath; the Circle would like to give one, and the Order would like them not to.

name: The Cistern of Isse
unique_feature: a Builders' cistern whose stair goes down into dry dark and sounds, all the way down, like water
story: The Builders stored water under their city and the Ash Winter drank it. The reedfolk say Isse of the Reeds walked up this stair out of the marsh, which is two regions away.
hook: Carry water from the Wellspring down the stair: something at the bottom wants to know whether it is still water.

name: The Kneeling Colossus
unique_feature: a fourteenth colossus kneeling on the rim with its hands over where its ears would be
story: The Choir has twelve and the Thirteenth walked away. This one stayed at the rim and covered its ears; the Order does not count it and will not say why.
hook: The Thirteenth's diggers want to dig this one too; the Order says a thing covering its ears has earned being left alone.

name: The Bell Garden
unique_feature: a Builders' garden of bells planted mouth-down in rows like cabbages, each a different note
story: When the Toll hums, the whole garden hums with it a half-note below, and the knights of the ring go and stand in the rows until it stops.
hook: Struck in the right order the garden plays a line, and the Cantor's Seat's door answers it.

name: Greywatch
unique_feature: three stones on the rim where the Order reads aloud the names of the ones who walked down
story: The Vigil Book says walk with them to the line. The line is below the rim; the stones are where the Order stops and reads, because a name read carries further than a walk.
hook: A name has been read at Greywatch every night for a month that is on no Chapter Roll.

name: The Ash-Winter Carts
unique_feature: a waystation roofless since the Ash Winter, its yard still full of the grain carts that were never unloaded
story: Then the roads west went under ash and the carts stopped coming. These are the carts: the grain is ash, the horses are bones in the traces, and the Order leaves them as they are.
hook: The carter's day-book lists a delivery to Greyfold made after the village had walked south.

name: The Bell Wood Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone in the White Wood, where pilgrims tie their bells to the dead ash trees before they walk south
story: Thousands of small bells hang in the dead wood and ring together in the dry wind. The pilgrims who tie them never come back for them, and nobody takes them down.
hook: Every bell in the wood is a person: the Wardens want the names written down, and the Order says the bells already are the names.

name: Ashcombe
unique_feature: a hamlet emptied in the Ash Winter whose chimneys still draw, though no fire has been lit in them for a hundred and seventy-seven years
story: Greyfold is remembered because of its tables. Ashcombe is not remembered at all, which is the worse end; the Wardens found it on an old tithe list and have not dared to put it back on the Roll.
encounter: ash-wights at the hearths after dark
hook: Put Ashcombe back on the Roll: find a name for each house, one chimney at a time.

name: Hesk Pool
unique_feature: Oroth steps going down into a still pool that gives back no reflection at all
story: Eelfathom Pool shows you a few seconds late; Hesk Pool does not show you at all. The Sayers call it the silence-water and take readings. Pilgrims do not look into it on the way south.
hook: The Sayers say Hesk Pool and Eelfathom are the same water, and that something stands in between.

name: The Last Milestone
unique_feature: three fused-stone milestones counting down to a harbour that is no longer there
story: The Builders' road west from the Choir ends in three markers: one, then none, then a stone with a word the Sayers read as shore. The sea is further west than that now.
hook: Walk the road the milestones count down and find the Builders' Harbour on the strand.

name: The Builders' Harbour
unique_feature: a Builders' quay whose steps go down into the Grey Sea and whose mooring posts are bells
story: Where the Builders' city met the sea. The Salt Isles traders would never moor here; they said the bells ring when a ship is coming that has not yet set out.
hook: The harbour bells rang last night; the reedfolk say a Salt Isles ship is due, and none has been seen in forty years.

name: The Grey Wreck
unique_feature: a Salt Isles salt-barge driven onto the Ash Strand and gone grey to the waterline
story: She came ashore in the Ash Winter with a hold of salt that had turned to ash on the voyage. Her crew walked inland and are on nobody's list.
encounter: ash-wights in the hold, still in their oilskins
hook: The barge's chart has the Salt Isles on it, and a line ruled from them to the Choir.

name: The Strand Beacon
unique_feature: a salt-traders' beacon of grey stone on the strand, its fire-bowl lit every night by nobody anyone has met
story: The Salt Isles traders built it to find the strand and stopped coming forty years ago. It burns every night anyway.
hook: Sit a night at the Strand Beacon and see who lights it.

name: The Ninth Waystone
unique_feature: three waystones on the road down from the West Downs with the Order's bell-count for every year scratched into them
story: Pilgrims coming down off the downs count the waystones. At the ninth they stop being Vale folk and start being pilgrims, and some of them sit on it for a while first.
hook: The bell-counts on the stone stop in 1024 and start again this spring, in a hand the Order does not know.

name: The Hermit's Gate
unique_feature: a Builders' gatehouse with a hermit's cell in its arch and a door with no hinges that he says he opened once
story: The hermit in the gate has lived on pilgrims' bread for thirty years. He is not mad, which is what makes people uneasy; he is waiting for the door to open again.
hook: The hermit says the door opens for a name, as the Undercroft's does, and he has been trying names for thirty years.

name: The Limekilns
unique_feature: three kilns at the foot of the Whitecut burning its chalk into the lime that whitewashes Tollmere
story: Every white wall in the city began as the Vale's hill. The burners work the kilns in shifts and are paid by the Tallymen by weight, which is the one thing everybody agrees is fair.
hook: The lime from the third kiln has come out grey, and the Tallymen want to know whether they can still sell it.

name: The Narrows Bridge
unique_feature: an Oroth arch over the mouth of the Skerrow Water, the first thing the North Road crosses on its way out of the heights
story: Clan carters coming down Kharrow Gorge cross the Narrows Bridge into the Tallymen's country. The arch has a clan mark cut on its north side and a guild mark on its south, and neither side admits to the other.
hook: The clan mark and the guild mark were both chiselled off the Narrows Bridge in the same night.

name: Gull Holm
unique_feature: an Oroth pier-house on an islet in the Mere, white with the gulls that nest in its windows
story: Nobody lands on Gull Holm except Merrowhithe's egg-collectors, once a spring, and they come back quiet. The pier-house has a door with no hinges that faces the city.
hook: The egg-collectors bring back one egg a year that is warm, from a room with no nest in it.

name: The Strandline Stones
unique_feature: three stones on the highest of the Mere's old shorelines, marking where the water stood the year the Toll fell
story: The Mere has fallen ten metres since the Toll came down and left its old beaches up the hillside like steps. The Sayers say it is draining; the Lakefolk say it is resting.
hook: A Sayer's measuring-rod stands by the stones: the water fell a finger's width this spring, the first change in a century.

name: The Listening Post
unique_feature: a Sayers' listening-tower on the east shore with a brass horn turned toward Merrowby to take the Toll's hum across the water
story: Ismay Ondrael's figures come from here: the Circle has taken the pitch of the hum every night for forty-one years from a room with a horn, a chair and a clerk who cannot sing.
hook: The clerk says the hum changed pitch on the night the Foundling came up the Stair.

name: The Tallyman's Folly
unique_feature: a Tallyman's summer house abandoned half-built when the Charter changed, the unpaid masons' names cut into the lintel
story: Guildmaster Pellow began it in 998 and stopped the day building became a paid service under the Charter. The masons cut their names into the lintel instead of their bill, which the Quiet Hands call the best receipt in Tollmere.
encounter: cutpurses use the cellars after dark
hook: The masons' names on the lintel are a debt the Tallymen never closed, and the Quiet Hands want it copied before the lintel is recut.

name: The Rafters' Camp
unique_feature: a timber camp at the Wold Water's mouth where Briarwold logs are lashed into rafts for the city
story: The Woodfolk float down what they will sell and not a stick more; the rafters pole it across to Tollmere's timber quay and complain about the Woodfolk the whole way.
hook: A raft came down the Wold Water with a forester tied to it, alive, silent, and not saying who.

name: The Stair Bridge
unique_feature: a stone bridge over Rudd Beck built from the steps of a Builders' stair somebody took apart
story: The north shore road crosses Rudd Beck here. On a still night the stones are said to count themselves, one to forty, and stop.
hook: A Merrowhithe mason says the stair went up to something before it was a bridge, and wants to know what.

name: The Fog Bell
unique_feature: a stilt-tower with a fog-bell rung every quarter hour while the fog is down, so the eel-boats can find the channel
story: The ringer is paid in eels by Moreva and Isseva both, and rings through the night whenever the fog is in, which is most nights. When the bell stops, the boats come in to find out why.
hook: The Fog Bell stopped last night, and the ringer is not in the tower.

name: The Long Jetty
unique_feature: a burial boardwalk running out into Lissane Mere, its last post hung with lanterns for the unmourned
story: Isseva buries its own from the town jetty. The Long Jetty is for the drowned who come up without a name; the reedfolk light a lantern for each and sing the third voice of the round.
encounter: bog-drowned climb to the last post at midnight
hook: Somebody has been leaving lanterns with names on them at the Long Jetty, and the names are all from the Vale.

name: The Peat Hags
unique_feature: a peat-cutters' camp on a drying island, the turves stacked like loaves around the fire
story: Peat from the south marsh warms Isseva, Nauve's Landing and half of Tollmere's poorer streets. The cutters find things in the peat, and are paid more for the finding than for the peat.
encounter: leech-hounds come up to the cuttings after dark
hook: The cutters have dug up a Warden, perfectly kept, with a roll of names in his hand; the Wardens and the Order both want him.

name: The Drowned Arch
unique_feature: an Oroth arch standing at the edge of Mormere with nothing on either side of it
story: The reedfolk say the arch was a door and the marsh was a room. Eel-boats pass under it for luck, and never through it the other way.
hook: An eel-boat went through the Drowned Arch the wrong way and came out at dawn with its crew a day older than they should be.

name: The Sunken Tower
unique_feature: a Builders' tower drowned to its third course, whose roof the reedfolk children dive from
story: Once a watch over a shore that is a mile out to sea now. The children dive from the top to touch the fourth course, which is carved with a face.
encounter: sallowjaws bask on the drowned courses
hook: The face carved on the fourth course is the face of the Thirteenth colossus.

name: The Traders' Post
unique_feature: the beach where Salt Isles traders drew up their boats and traded charts for indigo, their tent-poles still standing in the sand
story: The traders came every midsummer for three hundred years and stopped forty years ago without a word. Oulea still puts up one tent for them on the longest day.
hook: This midsummer a trader's chart was pinned to a tent-pole, and there was no boat on the sea.

name: The Eel-Boat Graveyard
unique_feature: eel-boats left to rot on the flats where the reedfolk say the drowned come ashore to count them
story: A reedfolk boat is never broken up; when it is done it is brought here and left to the tide. There are three hundred of them, and some of them have moved in the night.
encounter: bog-drowned walk among the hulls at night
hook: Ollo Nauve built one of the boats that moved, and wants it back where he left it.

name: Crookstilts
unique_feature: a hut on crooked stilts in the carr where the marsh-hag trades cures for names
story: The marsh-hag cures anything and takes a name in payment, not your own, one you know. The reedfolk go to her anyway, and do not say whose names they gave.
encounter: leech-hounds guard the stilts after dark
hook: The marsh-hag has Tessane's name, and will trade it.

name: The Indigo Beds
unique_feature: Isseva's north dye beds, where cloth is steeped in marsh indigo in long reed troughs
story: The only indigo in Wickmere comes up in these beds. This year it is coming up pale, and the dyers blame the fog, and Loa Oul blames the drowned.
hook: Find out where the indigo's colour is going: the dyers have noticed the pale beds are the ones nearest the Nave.

name: The Round Stones
unique_feature: three stones on three peat islets where the Round of Sa'oul is sung at midsummer, a choir on each
story: The round goes from stone to stone across the water, each voice starting as the last reaches the third line. It does not end; somebody stops, and then somebody else.
hook: Sing the second voice slightly flat on the fourth line and an old woman on the far islet begins to weep.

name: Mor'oul
unique_feature: a stilt-village sunk in a flood nobody recorded, its roof-ridges just under the water
story: The reedfolk put the drowned's apostrophe into its name the year it went under. The Tide account says a flood; there has never been a flood in any record, except here, in the name.
hook: Under the water Mor'oul's own lanterns are still lit.

name: Oskel Ford
unique_feature: an Oroth footbridge of column-drums laid across the Oskel where it comes down out of the heights into the fen
story: The only dry way from the clans' Oskeld Dale into the fen. Oskel miners carry lead down it to trade at Isseva, and the reedfolk never cross it the other way.
hook: Ore-carts have been found in the fen with the silver still aboard and the carters gone, and the Oskel clan want the ford watched.

name: The Northgate Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone facing the Briar's northern gate, whose wardstone still carries the Circle's chalk mark from 1038
story: The gate the Circle's Listeners went through. The chalk has not washed off in five years of rain, which the Woodfolk take as the gate's opinion of the Circle.
hook: The Circle wants the northern gate opened for a second expedition; Rookhold will not, and the northern gate has no keepers.

name: The Old Gate Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone facing the Old Gate, the one gate of the four whose doors still close
story: The keepers of Rookhold swear their oath at this stone with their backs to the gate, so that the last thing they see before they take the watch is the Wold.
hook: Every keeper has sworn facing the Wold; the youngest swore hers facing the gate, and the doors opened that night.

name: The Moot Gate Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone facing the Moot Gate, where the Briar is thickest and the Hart-Knights swear their vigil
story: The Hart-Knights kneel here before they take the antlers, facing the gate the Hart of Thorns is said to have come through.
hook: A Hart-Knight has knelt at the Moot Gate Stone three days and will not say what he is waiting for.

name: The Grey Man
unique_feature: a tor whose three topmost stones stand like old men in cloaks, looking west over the Wold
story: The Woodfolk say the Grey Man is three brothers who stood still to listen to the Standing Moot's hum and forgot to stop.
hook: From the top of the Grey Man the Moot's hum is audible, and it has a word in it.

name: Hollin Tor
unique_feature: a holly-grown tor crowned with leaning stones where the Woodfolk hang the unstrung bows of their dead
story: When a woodfolk hunter dies their bow is unstrung and hung on Hollin Tor. There are a thousand bows. None has ever been restrung.
hook: One of the bows on Hollin Tor has been restrung.

name: Wold Force
unique_feature: the Wold Water dropping in a single rope of white down a granite step, with a stone bench cut into the rock beside it
story: Fernhold's foresters settle arguments at Wold Force: whoever can sit longest on the bench in the spray without speaking wins.
hook: Alder Wyke and a Sayer have been sitting on the bench at Wold Force for two days.

name: Blackgill Falls
unique_feature: three falls stepping down the granite stair through a gill so overhung with oak it is dark at noon
story: Weavers breed in Blackgill's dark. The Northwold's woodfolk throw a lit torch down each fall before they go past it.
hook: A woodfolk child fell into Blackgill and came up in the Mere two days later, dry.

name: Barkbridge
unique_feature: a woodfolk bridge of three bark-roofed spans on granite piers, the only covered bridge in Wickmere
story: The Wold roofs its bridges so a traveller caught by rain has somewhere to stand without asking anybody's leave. Leave is not asked in the Wold; shelter is simply there.
hook: A poacher sleeps under Barkbridge's roof every night and nobody moves him on, because that is the custom, and he is counting on it.

name: The Antler Chapel
unique_feature: a roofless hall where the Hart-Knights hang the antlers of every hart they have killed, in the Hart's memory
story: The Hart-Knights' chapel was a woodfolk lodge until the knights took the antlers up. The Woodfolk say the knights are mourners who have forgotten what for.
hook: A knight asks for the antlers the poachers sold in Tollmere as Oroth relics to be brought back.

name: The Antler Boilers
unique_feature: a poachers' camp where hart antlers are sawn and boiled to pass for Oroth relics in the Tollmere market
story: The Hunters' Stand's poachers do their butchery here, as far from the lodges as the Wold allows. The Woodfolk know, and have said nothing, which is the custom and a mistake.
hook: The Ledger of Prices lists Oroth antler at forty marks; the boilers' account book lists it at two.

name: The Sawpit
unique_feature: a sawpit under a trestle where two sawyers have not spoken in eleven years and never missed a stroke
story: Top-man and pit-man, brothers, sawing the Wold's planks for Tamwick's carts. They fell out over a woman who married neither, and the saw has done their talking since.
hook: One brother asks for a message to be carried down the pit to the other.

name: Mossgrave
unique_feature: a woodfolk burial ground where the dead are laid under moss and each grave's moss is given their name
story: The Woodfolk bury without stones: a body under a named moss, and the moss tended until nobody remembers the name, which is when the moss is let go.
encounter: a Warden stands among the mounds
hook: One moss has been let go that somebody still remembers.

name: The Wardstone Line
unique_feature: a line of broken Oroth wardstones running back from the Briar into the wood, as if the thorn once stood here
story: The Briar has moved. The Circle says the Builders grew it further out; the Woodfolk say it stood further in and has crept east for nine hundred years, away from something.
hook: Measure the line against the Briar and settle which way it has moved.

name: Harrow Tor
unique_feature: a granite tor whose top is a cairn of every stone the northern gate's keepers ever cleared from the road
story: The northern gate had keepers once. They cleared the road each morning and carried every stone up here. Nobody has cleared the road since the Chain Years.
hook: The road to the northern gate is clear again every morning, and there are no keepers.

name: The Skarl Bridge
unique_feature: a granite bridge where the Wold's north road crosses the Skarl Water into clan country, a woodfolk bow-knot cut in one parapet and a clan mark in the other
story: The border between custom and blood-price is the middle of this bridge. Travellers pay the clan toll on one side and ask the Woodfolk's leave on the other, and the wise do both twice.
hook: Somebody has been paying blood-price at the middle of the bridge for a death on the Woodfolk side.

name: The Sentinels
unique_feature: three leaning granite stones in a clearing where the wardens gather at dusk and stand as if listening
story: The wardens, the Wold's walking trees, gather here at dusk and stand among the stones until dawn. The Woodfolk do not cut within bowshot of the clearing.
hook: The wardens have started standing at the Sentinels by day as well, all facing the Briar.

name: The Old Quarry
unique_feature: a granite quarry where the Builders cut the stone for the Long Stride, its last block still hanging half-cut from the face
story: The quarrymen's marks are the causeway's marks. Tollmere does not like to be reminded that its famous Oroth causeway came out of a wood it calls savage.
hook: The half-cut block has Oroth writing on its hidden face: the Stride's own dedication, never laid.

name: Countwatch
unique_feature: a squat granite watch-tower on a tor, its walls chalked with the tally of grey patches on the Briar, nineteen and counting
story: Fernhold's foresters climb it every morning to count the grey patches in the thorn. Fourteen at midwinter, nineteen now; the chalk will run out before the wall does.
hook: The count went down by one overnight; the patch did not heal, it moved.

name: The Silked Camp
unique_feature: a woodfolk hunting camp abandoned in one night and strung over since with weaver silk, the bedrolls still in the tents
story: Six hunters from Ormhold slept here eleven years ago and were not found. The weavers have kept the camp as a larder, and the Woodfolk have left it as a warning.
hook: Six hunters' bows are missing from Hollin Tor's thousand; the Wold counts them as hung.

name: Kharrow Gate
unique_feature: a clan gate-tower at the mouth of Kharrow Gorge where the North Road enters the heights and blood-price begins
story: Travellers are told the law here: what is taken is paid for in kind, a death in blood-price, and a host is never robbed. The gate-ward asks each traveller to say it back.
hook: A traveller refused to say the law back and walked on; the clans want to know what she is.

name: Ghast's Broken Bridge
unique_feature: a chain bridge across Ghast Dale with one chain cut, hanging askew in the gorge since the year of the broken bridge
story: The chain Ghast cut was Kharrow's. Nobody has crossed in two hundred years, except goats, who do not know about the Moot.
encounter: crag-wolves den under the anchor stones
hook: Cross it, and read the mark on the far anchor that belongs to no clan.

name: Brindle Swallow
unique_feature: three cairns round a swallow-hole where Brindle Beck drops out of the world and is heard a mile underground
story: The beck falls into the hole and comes out a day later and colder at Brindlecrag's spring. The miners say it passes the singing shaft on the way.
hook: Drop a bell into Brindle Swallow and listen for it at Brindlecrag's spring.

name: The Smeltings
unique_feature: Brindle's smelting kilns below the village, the ore-carts drawn up by their mouths
story: Iron from the top of the vein, lead from the middle and silver from the bottom, which is smelted at night with the doors shut and the pipes playing.
hook: The silver has come out of the kiln with a ring in it, and struck it hums a note the smiths refuse to name.

name: Old Eld
unique_feature: an abandoned silver working on the edge, its shaft sealed with a door of bone
story: The first silver working on Brindle Edge, sealed when the singing started at Oskeld. The bone door is a giant's shoulder-blade, and it is warm.
encounter: a stone-thrall walks the working after dark
hook: Open the bone door at Old Eld.

name: The Jawbone
unique_feature: a giant's jaw standing on end like a gate at the head of Oskeld Dale, the rest of the skull sunk in the moor
story: Oskel herds go through the Jawbone every spring on the way up and every autumn on the way down. A beast that balks is sold, not eaten.
encounter: crag-wolves wait in the heather beyond it
hook: Every beast in a herd balked at the Jawbone this spring.

name: The Giant's Spine
unique_feature: a giant's spine lying along the head of Ribdale with a clan cairn raised on every vertebra
story: The clans say the Rib Cathedral's ribs belong to this spine, which would make the giant a mile long. The Sayers say two giants. The clans say the Sayers have not counted the vertebrae.
encounter: stone-thralls stand up among the vertebrae
hook: Count the vertebrae.

name: Kharrow Force
unique_feature: the Skerrow Water leaping in one fall into the head of Kharrow Gorge, a rope of iron links strung across its lip for the brave to cross
story: Kharrow youths cross the lip on their naming day. The ones who fall are fished out at the Hold, a mile down, and are named anyway, but differently.
hook: Cross the lip of Kharrow Force and the clans will name you for it.

name: Rudd Pike Beacon
unique_feature: a clan beacon on Rudd Pike whose fire-bowl is lit when the Windgate avalanche comes down
story: When the Long Snow slides on the Windgate, Rudd Pike burns and every hold shuts its doors. It burned for the winter of the long snow, and Rudd have not let anybody forget it.
hook: Rudd Pike Beacon burned last night, and the Windgate snow did not move.

name: The Snow Shelter
unique_feature: a stone shelter on the Windgate road with a bell on a pole for travellers caught by the weather
story: The gate-warden keeps it stocked with peat and oatcake. The bell is rung by anyone caught out, and whoever hears it goes, which is the one law older than the Moot.
hook: The shelter bell rang on a clear night, and whoever rang it was gone when the gate-warden came.

name: Kharrow's Cairns
unique_feature: three memory-cairns above the gorge where every Kharrow who died on the mountain is named once a year
story: Ushka ko-Kharrow kept the memory forty-one years and lost no name; these are the cairns she sang them at.
hook: Dunna ko-Kharrow wants the cairns' names checked against the Rope-Song, and one of them is not in it.

name: The Blood-Price Stones
unique_feature: three stones by the North Road with grooves worn in their tops where blood-price is paid in laid coin
story: A clan owed a death is paid here, in public, on the road, so every traveller sees that it was. The coin lies in the grooves a day before it is taken up.
hook: There is coin in the grooves for a death nobody has reported.

name: The Giants' Stair
unique_feature: a stair of steps each as high as a man, cut up the wall toward the north by something with longer legs
story: The giants' last road, the clans say, going north past the Windgate into the Ice Reach. It stops at a sheer face where the snow has never melted.
encounter: a stone-thrall sits on the top step
hook: Climb to where the Giants' Stair stops and read what is cut in the last riser.

name: The Bonefield
unique_feature: a scree slope where giant bones lie as thick as fallen timber, bleached and furred with lichen
story: Skarl herders gather bone here for lintels and tokens. They take only what has come loose on its own, and leave a stone for each piece.
encounter: stone-thralls rise out of the scree
hook: The Bonefield's bones have started to lie in order.

name: Ghorrow
unique_feature: an eighth hold cut into the cliff with no clan's mark over its door, and eight doors inside, seven of them bricked
story: The clans say Ghorrow is a cave. The Rope-Song has a breath where an eighth verse should be. The one open door inside goes down.
hook: Ghorr, the Bone Clan: the hold that kept their name, and the door that goes down to whoever is holding it.

name: Skarl Shieling
unique_feature: a summer shieling of turf huts on the high fell, where Skarl's herders sing the cattle down at dusk
story: The herders live up here from thaw to first snow and sing the cattle down each dusk with the Skarl verse. The cattle know the tune better than the words.
hook: The cattle came down at dusk to a verse nobody sang.

name: Oskel Shieling
unique_feature: a herders' shieling at the head of Oskeld Dale whose peat-fire is kept in all year for the mine's sake
story: Oskel keep a fire burning at the dale head the year round so the mine can see it. They say it is for the herders; the herders say it is for the mine.
hook: The shieling fire went out, and for a night the mine's singing stopped.

name: Skarl Spout
unique_feature: a waterfall that pours out of a hole halfway up a limestone scar, with no stream above it
story: The Skarl Water runs under the moor and comes out of the cliff's face. The Skarl verse says the giants drank here; the Sayers say karst.
hook: Something came out of Skarl Spout with the water: a clan token of no clan.

name: Ruddale Bridge
unique_feature: a limestone arch over Rudd Beck with a Rudd herd-mark cut on every stone
story: Rudd built it so their herds could come down to the Mere's grazing without paying Kharrow's toll at the gorge. Kharrow has never said a word about it, which is how Kharrow says a great deal.
hook: Kharrow's toll-keeper has started standing on Ruddale Bridge, saying nothing.

name: The Red Moor
unique_feature: leaning stones on the moor where Ghast and Kharrow fought in the year of the broken bridge, one stone for each of the dead
story: The one battle in the Rope-Song, and it is sung as a debt, not a victory. Heather grows red on the moor there and nowhere else in the heights.
hook: A new stone stands on the Red Moor, and nobody has died.

name: The Skerry Watch
unique_feature: a drystone look-out on the sea cliff above the Skerries, where Oskel wives watched for the Salt Isles boats
story: The Salt Isles traders came round the north cape to Oskelcrag once, for lead. The look-out is kept swept, though nobody has watched from it in forty years.
hook: Somebody has been sweeping the Skerry Watch, and leaving the broom.

name: The Roll Stone
unique_feature: a single standing stone at the foot of Wardens' Down with the four quiet villages cut into it and struck through
story: The Wardens read the Roll aloud here on Candle Night, name by name, and strike nothing: the four names were struck through by the hands that cut them.
hook: A fifth name has been cut beneath the four in a Warden's hand, and struck through, and nobody at the Rest will say whose.

name: The Old Sheepwash
unique_feature: a drystone wash-pool dammed across a dry spring-head, the sheep-gate still hung
story: Fallowfold's flocks were washed here before shearing for three hundred years. The spring went up the hill in the year Wynstead's meadows drowned, and the shepherds have carried buckets after it since.
hook: The spring is moving again, a yard a day, toward Fallowfold's gate.

name: The Pinfold
unique_feature: a round drystone pound for strayed beasts beside the Eastway, with a hand-bell hung on its gate
story: Merrowby's hayward pens the Vale's strays here until their owners pay a penny, ring the bell and take them home.
hook: Every morning there is one more sheep in the Pinfold than anybody put there, and nobody in the Vale will own it.

name: The Dewpond Fold
unique_feature: a shepherds' summer fold round a dew pond that nobody has ever seen empty or filling
story: Barrow Down's flocks are folded here from Naming Day to the Long Table and drink from the one water on the down that nobody dug.
hook: On still nights the dew pond shows the stars at noon, and the shepherds have stopped mentioning it.

name: The Hare Stone
unique_feature: a boundary stone with a hare cut on its Vale face and an oak leaf on its Wold face, both worn smooth by hands
story: Where the downs end and the Wold begins. Vale folk touch the hare going in and Woodfolk touch the leaf coming out; nobody has ever been seen to touch both.
hook: Somebody has cut a third mark on the top of the stone overnight, a bell, and left the chisel in the grass.

name: Tallow Barrow
unique_feature: a long barrow opened by treasure-diggers and walled up again from the inside
story: Diggers from Tollmere opened it in 1012 for grave-gold the Vale swears was never there. They came out without their spades and would not go back, and in the morning the entrance was walled.
encounter: hedge-wights come out of the barrow at night
hook: The new wall has a door-shaped gap in it this spring, and the chalk round the gap is warm.

name: The Warrener's Camp
unique_feature: a warrener's turf hut and ferret-hutches dug into the gorse under the Thornmarch
story: Rookdown's warrener keeps the downs' rabbits in check and sells their skins in Tamwick. He has not been seen at home since the Long Table.
encounter: none; the warrener's things and nobody home
hook: The ferrets will not go down one burrow, and every rabbit on the down comes out of it.

name: The Cliff Hearth
unique_feature: a Hearthstone on the Brow's last rise, with a fire kept for whoever comes up from the Hush
story: The Vale says the fire was lit for the drowned; the Wardens say it was lit for the Foundlings, before the Foundlings stopped coming. Rookdown keeps it because it has always been kept.
hook: The ash was warm on the morning the Foundling came up the Stair, and nobody on the Brow had lit it.

name: The Hush Steps
unique_feature: Oroth steps cut down the face of the Brow's cliff and stopping in the air above the water
story: Nobody knows what the Builders went down to. Rookdown's children dare each other to the last step, and the last step is always one further down than the last child reached.
hook: A lit lantern has been left on the last step, tied with a Sedgish lantern-knot.

name: The Cliff Graves
unique_feature: a row of graves along the cliff's edge, every headstone turned to face the Hush
story: Rookdown buries its drowned here, facing the water that took them, so they will see it coming if it comes back for the rest.
hook: One headstone has turned in the night to face inland.

name: Rook Mill
unique_feature: a sail-less windmill on the Brow's back whose millstone is heard grinding on still nights
story: Rookdown's mill lost its sails in the gale of 1030 and was never rigged again. The miller moved down to the village; the millstone stayed.
hook: Flour has been found on the mill floor, fine and grey, and it tastes of ash.

name: Candle Cross
unique_feature: a wayside Hearthstone where the Brow road crosses the drove, with a candle niche cut in each of its four faces
story: On Candle Night every farm on the Brow sends one candle here, and the crossroads is the brightest place on the downs until dawn.
hook: A candle has been burning in the north niche since midsummer, and it has not got any shorter.

name: The Last Look
unique_feature: a leaning stone and a pilgrims' bench on the last of the downs, looking out over the ash to the Choir
story: Pilgrims leaving the Vale stop here for their last look at green ground. Pilgrims coming back touch the stone and do not look round.
hook: The stone leans a little further toward the Choir every year; this year it moved a hand's breadth in one night.

name: Pennywort Bridge
unique_feature: a humpback bridge over the Larkbourne with a cracked millstone set in its parapet
story: The mill's first stone cracked on its first turn and was built into the bridge, so the Larkbourne would carry the bad luck down to the Mere.
hook: The cracked millstone has turned a quarter in the parapet, and there is fresh mortar dust in the road.

name: The Wash-Stones
unique_feature: three flat stones at the water's edge where Tollmere's washing is beaten, each worn into a dish
story: Tollmere's laundresses come over the Stride twice a week because the water here is soft. The stones are older than the city; the laundresses say the Builders did their washing too.
hook: A shirt came up in the wash that none of the laundresses brought: a Sayer's, with a name in the collar that the Circle unsaid.

name: The Sedge Hearth
unique_feature: a Hearthstone on a peat island in the reeds, reached by a single plank
story: Sedgehithe's cutters built it where the Lakefolk and the reedfolk quarrelled over the reed-beds, so that both would have to share one fire.
hook: The plank to the island has been taken up, from the island side.

name: The Dry Jetty
unique_feature: a boardwalk jetty standing in a hayfield two hundred yards from the water, where the Mere used to reach
story: Gullhithe's old landing, left high in one lifetime as the Mere fell. The eel-wives still walk out along it at dusk, from habit.
hook: Every morning this spring the jetty's last pile has been wet to the knee, and the field round it dry.

name: The Eggers' Camp
unique_feature: tents and rope-coils at the top of the Gull Cliffs, where Gullhithe's egg-collectors go over on ropes
story: Every spring Gullhithe goes over the cliff on ropes for the gulls' eggs, and every spring somebody's rope is found cut.
hook: This year the cut rope was cut from below.

name: The Charter Stone
unique_feature: the stone the first Charter was cut on, broken by the clans and mended with brass pins
story: Where the clans and the Tallymen agreed in 712 that the North Road would be free of toll above the Narrows and of blood-price below them. Both sides have broken it since, and both still come here to swear.
hook: The brass pins are being drawn out, one a night, and there are two left.

name: Brindle Mill
unique_feature: a clan grist-mill on Brindle Beck whose mill wheel turns against the water
story: Brindlecrag's lowland mill, where the clans grind the barley they buy from the Vale. The miller is clanless and pays nobody.
hook: The wheel turns against the current, and for a stride below the mill the beck runs uphill.

name: The Counting Tower
unique_feature: a Tallymen's tower where the North Road's carts were counted before the Charter freed the road, every window bricked but one
story: The Tallymen still keep a clerk here, counting the carts that come down out of Skerrow for a tax nobody has paid since 942.
hook: The clerk has stopped counting; the tower's ledger is being kept by someone else, in Oroth numerals.

name: The Standing Arches
unique_feature: a run of the Builders' aqueduct striding over the cliff-top toward Merrowhithe, broken at both ends
story: Water never ran in it in anyone's memory. Merrowhithe's smokehouses are hung in its last arches, down at the shore.
hook: The channel along its top is wet this spring from end to end, and drips at the break.

name: The Beached Barge
unique_feature: a Woodfolk timber barge the Mere left high and dry, with an oak growing up through its hold
story: Beached when the water fell in 1005, with her last cargo still lashed. Nobody has claimed the timber: the Woodfolk say it was never paid for and the Tallymen say it was never delivered.
hook: The oak growing through the hold is older than the barge.

name: The Log Boom
unique_feature: a boom of chained logs across the Wold Water, walked like a bridge by the rafters
story: The rafters make up their rafts behind the boom and let them go one at a time, so that the Mere is not all logs at once.
hook: A raft was let go with nobody on it, and it went up the Wold Water, not down.

name: The Lime Bridge
unique_feature: a whitewashed bridge over the Cressbourne's mouth, limed so often it is more lime than stone
story: The lime-burners whitewash it every spring with the first burn, for luck, and the Tallymen charge the kilns for the lime.
hook: This spring the bridge came up grey under the whitewash, like the third kiln's lime, and the white will not take.

name: Saoul
unique_feature: a ring of empty stilts standing in a black pool, a lit lantern hung on every one
story: The lantern-pool, named for Sa'oul, who is in it. The village that stood here moved to Saeva a hundred years ago and left its lanterns for her.
encounter: wisps over the pool at night
hook: The lanterns are relit every night, and the reedfolk swear that none of them does it.

name: The Greyreed Decoy
unique_feature: a wildfowlers' decoy of netted channels cut into the reeds, with a screen of wattle for the decoyman
story: Nauvissa's decoyman draws the Greyreed's ducks up the netted pipes with a dog and a song. He sells every bird to Tollmere and eats none of them.
encounter: none; a decoyman and his dog
hook: The decoy dog has started leading something else up the pipes at night, and the nets are torn from inside.

name: The Salt Pans
unique_feature: square brine pools on the tideflats drying white in rows, and the salt-rakers' huts on legs
story: The only salt in Wickmere that is not carried down from the Skerrow mines. The reedfolk trade it for lamp-oil and say the sea is giving back what it owes.
hook: A pan dried to a crust overnight with footprints across it from the sea side, and none coming back.

name: The Tide Hearth
unique_feature: a Hearthstone on the Outfall's south bank hung round with lantern-knots, one for every name the water has taken
story: Reedfolk who have lost someone to the water come here to tie a knot and say the name once. The Sayers call it superstition; the Tallymen charge nothing to pass it, which is the most respect Tollmere has.
hook: A knot has been tied for a name nobody in Sedgemire knows, and it stays dry in the spray.

name: The Old Crannog
unique_feature: an island-house of wattle on a heap of stones in the carr, older than any stilt in Sedgemire
story: The reedfolk say their grandmothers' grandmothers lived on islands before Isse taught them stilts. The crannog is the last one, and nobody sleeps in it twice.
encounter: leech-hounds in the carr at night
hook: Somebody has been sleeping in it every night, and leaves the fire laid for the next.

name: The Knuckle Cairn
unique_feature: a clan cairn on the last dry stone before the fen, capped with a giant's knuckle-bone
story: The Oskel clan's boundary. Past it, the clans say, is not their memory's business.
hook: The knuckle-bone has been turned to point into the fen, which in clan sign means follow.

name: The Drowned Road
unique_feature: an Oroth road of fused stone running straight out of the carr and into the sea
story: The Builders' road west, cut off where the sea took the land. The reedfolk say it goes on under the water to the Salt Isles, and the Salt Isles traders say it arrives.
hook: At the lowest tide this spring the road showed a milestone further out than anyone had seen, cut with a number.

name: The Grey Gull
unique_feature: a Salt Isles trading ship driven onto the carr's edge, her figurehead a gull with a woman's face
story: She came ashore in the storm of 1031 with nobody aboard and her boats still lashed. The reedfolk have taken nothing from her, because a ship that comes without its crew has come for someone.
hook: The figurehead's face has been recognised: a reedfolk woman of Moreva, alive, who has never been to sea.

name: The Boardwalk Gate
unique_feature: a reedfolk gate of lantern-hung posts where the Westway leaves the downs and goes onto a boardwalk over the delta
story: Nauvissa keeps the gate and lights it every dusk, so that the Vale's carters know where the ground stops.
hook: The lanterns were found lit at noon, and the boardwalk wet with footprints coming out of the delta.

name: The Reed Bridge
unique_feature: a footbridge of bundled reed over a creek, a new one laid on the old every spring
story: Nobody has taken the old bridge down in two hundred years; the reedfolk lay the new one on top, and the bridge stands higher every year.
hook: The bridge has sunk to the water overnight, two hundred years of reed pressed flat as if something very heavy had crossed.

name: The Eel Hurdles
unique_feature: the eel-trappers' summer raft of huts moored among wattle hurdles that steer the eels into the traps
story: Oulea's trappers live out on the water from thaw to first frost and come ashore only for burials.
hook: Every morning the traps are full of eels swimming the wrong way, out to sea.

name: The Wading Giant
unique_feature: a giant's ribs and hips standing out of the sea-cliff where the waves have eaten the land away
story: The Oskel clan say the giant walked into the sea to drown the Breath in him, and got as far as his hips.
hook: Each winter's storms uncover more of him, and this winter they uncovered a hand, closed on something.

name: The Frost Moot
unique_feature: a ring of stone seats in a hollow under the Wall where the seven clans met before the Rib Cathedral, with one seat more than seven
story: The Old Moot. The clans stopped meeting here when they could no longer agree how many seats to sweep.
hook: The snow is brushed off one seat every morning, and it is never the same seat twice.

name: The Oskel Rake
unique_feature: a lead-miners' trench cut a mile along the dale-side, with a winding-stone at its head
story: Oskelcrag's lead came out of the rake before the singing shaft was found. The miners left the rake when it began to answer their picks.
encounter: stone-thralls work the rake at night
hook: Picks are heard in the rake at night, and every morning another yard of the vein is open.

name: The Breathing Stones
unique_feature: a ring of standing stones round a shakehole on the moor that draws the air in and lets it out like a sleeper
story: The clans come here to hear the Breath. Children are held over the hole to be breathed on for luck, and the ones who are not afraid are told they will be herders.
hook: The hole has stopped breathing out.

name: The Rope Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn on Brindle Edge hung with children's ropes, taller than a man
story: Brindle children are roped to the fell until they can walk the Edge alone. The outgrown rope goes on the cairn, and the cairn has outgrown the oldest herder on the Edge.
hook: A rope has been added that no Brindle family owns, knotted in a fashion nobody has tied for two hundred years.

name: Kharrow Foot
unique_feature: a walled market-field at the foot of the fells where the clans trade with the lowlands, with a bell-post in the middle
story: Skerrow does not let Tollmere's carts up the gorge on market days; the lowlands come to Kharrow Foot instead, and pay blood-price for any quarrel inside the wall.
encounter: none; clan traders with jobs going
hook: The bell-post rang on a day with no market, and every clan came down to answer it.

name: The Bone Ford
unique_feature: a giant's backbone laid across Rib Beck, walked as stepping-stones
story: The Rib Cathedral's giant lost his spine coming down the dale, the clans say, and the beck has been crossing it ever since.
hook: The vertebrae have been counted at thirty-one for a thousand years; this spring there are thirty-two.

name: The Tappers' Camp
unique_feature: a resin-tappers' camp in the Rib Pines, a clay pot hung on every trunk
story: The clans tap the pines for the pitch that keeps their chain-links from rusting.
hook: The resin in one stand of pines has come out red, and the tappers will not go near it.

name: The Rust Scar
unique_feature: a limestone scar in Ruddale's side where the water comes out of the rock the colour of rust
story: Ruddow washes its dead's hands in it before burial. The Rudd clan say the fell is bleeding for its giants.
hook: The water ran clear for one day this spring, and every Rudd child born that day has been named for it.

name: The Deadground
unique_feature: grey spoil heaps and roofless ore-sheds below Oskeld Mine, where nothing has grown in a hundred years
story: The mine's waste was tipped here until the goats that grazed it started walking into the shaft.
hook: Grass has begun to grow on the Deadground, in a single line, toward the mine.

name: Ghastfoot
unique_feature: the Ghast clan's arch at the mouth of their dale, with a skull set in the keystone
story: Travellers going up Ghast Dale ask leave of the skull. The ones who do not ask are the ones who come back down in a hurry.
hook: The skull has been taken from the keystone and a clay one left in its place, very well painted.

name: The Drove Chain
unique_feature: two stones on the Low Road with an iron chain slung between them, which the drovers lift for the herds
story: The Ghast and Brindle clans agreed the chain in 1001: a herd passing pays a beast, and a traveller pays a piece of news.
hook: The chain was found lifted and the price paid in news: a name, spoken to the chain-ward by someone he cannot now describe.

name: The Tinkers' Camp
unique_feature: a clanless tinkers' winter camp under the end of Oskel Edge, pots and chains hung ringing from a frame of bones
story: The tinkers mend the clans' pots and chains and belong to nobody. The clans let them winter here because a tinker is the only news that walks.
hook: The tinkers are packing to leave early, and say only that the chains have been ringing with no wind.

name: The Skerr Stone
unique_feature: a broken waystone at the fells' foot, cut in Skerrish on one face and Valish on the other, the Valish chiselled away
story: The first stone of the clans' country on the Low Road. The Brindle clan cut the Valish off in the Charter quarrel of 942 and never put it back.
hook: The Valish has been cut back in overnight, badly, in a hand like a child copying letters.

name: The Clan Stones
unique_feature: seven painted stones on the fellside, one for each clan, and an eighth socket standing empty
story: Where the Moot swore its first peace. Each clan's stone is painted at midsummer by its eldest; nobody paints round the empty socket, and it is always painted.
hook: A stone has been found standing in the eighth socket, unpainted, and no clan will touch it.

name: The Briar's End
unique_feature: the gap where the Thornmarch's briar gives out against the fell, walled across with bones
story: The one place the Thornmarch is not briar. The Woodfolk walled it and the Skarl clan keeps the wall, and neither will say what from.
hook: The bone wall has been pushed outward in the night, from this side.

name: The Watcher
unique_feature: a giant's skull half out of the scree under the Wall, as big as a barn, looking east
story: The Skarl clan say he died watching the Thornmarch, waiting for something to come through it.
encounter: a scree-hag nests in the skull
hook: The skull has turned in the scree, a hand's breadth south, toward the rest of Wickmere.

name: The Black Keep
unique_feature: a clan tower at Skarldale's narrows, burned by two clans at once and left black
story: The Skarl and the Rudd fought over the dale's summer grass for sixty years. The Moot ended it by giving the grass to neither; the keep was burned by both on the same night, and each still says the other lit it first.
hook: Somebody has been relaying the keep's stair stone by stone, at night, and the Moot wants to know which clan.

name: The Winter Cairns
unique_feature: a fellside of small cairns over the herds lost in the Long Winter of 988, one cairn for every beast
story: The Skarl clan count their wealth in these as well as in their living herds: a beast remembered is a beast still owned.
hook: Every morning this month a pebble has been added to every cairn, and there are four thousand cairns.

name: The Verderer's Tower
unique_feature: a Woodfolk lookout built round a living trunk high over the High Wold's canopy
story: The Woodfolk's only watch on the east. The verderer counts harts and fires, and the fires have been fewer every year.
hook: The verderer saw a fire on the far side of the Thornmarch, outside the world, and has not come down since.

name: The Briar Nursery
unique_feature: the Woodfolk's briar nursery, beds of Thornmarch cuttings in rows under the rampart and a gardener's hut
story: When the Thornmarch thins, the Woodfolk plant it thick again from here. It is the one garden in the Briarwold and the one work nobody volunteers for.
hook: The cuttings have begun to lean east, every one, as if the sun were outside.

name: The Poachers' Lee
unique_feature: a poachers' camp in the lee of the Thornmarch, deer-hides pegged on frames and a bow-rack
story: The Woodfolk know where the camp is. Custom says they may not burn it until the poachers are in it.
hook: The poachers have gone in a hurry and left their catch: a hart with antlers of bone-white wood.

name: The Knight's Mound
unique_feature: a Hart-Knight's grave-mound in the Greatwood, his antlered helm set on top and grown into the roots
story: The Hart-Knights kept the Wold before the Woodfolk came; the last of them was buried here and the wood grew over him. The Woodfolk leave him a cup of water at midwinter.
hook: The cup was drunk from this midwinter.

name: The Tally Hearth
unique_feature: a Hearthstone at a forest crossing hung with Woodfolk tally-sticks, a notch for every tree taken
story: Woodfolk custom: a tree taken is a notch cut, and a notch cut is a tree planted by the next spring. The sticks are the Wold's only ledger.
hook: The notches outnumber the new trees by forty this spring, and the Woodfolk want to know who has been cutting.

name: The Bark Camp
unique_feature: oak trunks stripped white and left standing, the bark drying on racks for Tamwick's tanners
story: The Woodfolk sell bark, never timber. The stripped oaks are left to die standing, which the Woodfolk say is kinder than the axe.
hook: One stripped oak has grown its bark back in a week.

name: Pellow's Pale
