unique_feature: the wall of a Tallyman's deer-park falling down in the Lower Wold, its gate still locked
story: Guildmaster Pellow walled a deer-park here in 996, and the Woodfolk let the harts out through the wall the night it was finished. The wall has been falling down politely ever since.
hook: The gate has been unlocked from inside, with a key the Tallymen swear was never cut.

name: The Foxgill Arch
unique_feature: a natural granite arch over the Foxgill gorge, with Woodfolk railings along it
story: The Woodfolk did not build it and will not say who did; they only put the railings on.
hook: The railings have been cut through on the Fernhold side.

name: The Hush Bell
unique_feature: a bell-tower on the cliff's edge whose bell hangs out over the Hush on a stone arm
story: The pilgrims rang it for the ships that brought them. No ship has come since the Stair was cut, and the rope has rotted to a hand's length.
hook: The bell has been rung: the rope is new, and wet with sea-water.

name: The Tenth Waystone
unique_feature: a pilgrims' waystone with ten notches in its edge and a bowl worn in its top for coins
story: The waystones count on from the Vale toward the Choir, and the pilgrims leave a coin in each bowl. The tenth's is always empty by morning.
hook: The coins taken from the tenth waystone turn up in the fire at the Stair Head, melted.

name: The Row of Mouths
unique_feature: a colonnade of Oroth pillars, each carved as an open mouth, running west from the Choir into the ash
story: The Builders' processional way from the Choir to their city. The pilgrims walk it with their mouths shut.
encounter: choristers walk the colonnade at night
hook: At dusk one mouth is heard singing a single note, a different pillar every night, and the Order is counting which.

name: Hesk-Morn
unique_feature: an Oroth door with no hinges standing upright on the cliff's edge, opening on the Hush
story: The pilgrims call it the Silent Door and will not walk between it and the sea. The Order says the Builders stood in it to listen to the Hush.
hook: The door has been found open, and the ash beyond it holds footprints that walk out onto the air.

name: The Silent Market
unique_feature: a market square of the dead city with its stalls still standing in fused stone, the goods on them all ash
story: The pilgrims will not cross it by day and the Ashgrid's scavengers will not cross it by night. Nobody says what is sold there.
hook: One stall at the edge of the square has fresh goods on it every morning: bread, a knife, a child's shoe.

name: Sulion
unique_feature: the dead city's harbour light, its lamp-socket empty and staring out to sea
story: The Builders' harbour light. Its sul-stone is the one in the Lamp at Gullhithe, carried across Wickmere by Tallymen in 998 and never paid for.
hook: The empty socket glows on moonless nights, and on those nights the Lamp at Gullhithe dims.

name: The North Gate
unique_feature: the dead city's north gate, a fused-stone arch standing alone with no wall left either side of it
story: The pilgrims walk through it rather than round it; out of courtesy, the Order says.
hook: Something passes through the gate at the same hour every night, leaving the ash disturbed and no tracks.

name: The Greyline Stones
unique_feature: a line of chalk stones marking where the grey begins, each one set a little further back than the one before
story: The Wardens set a stone at the edge of the ash every Naming Day. Every year the ash has come a few yards on, and the new stone goes in behind it.
hook: This year's stone was set in front of last year's: the ash has gone back.

name: The Driftwood Camp
unique_feature: a strand-scavengers' camp roofed with driftwood and a ship's ribs
story: The Ash Strand's scavengers live off what the Grey Sea brings in, which is less every year.
hook: The sea brought in a Tollmere barge last week with her cargo sealed and her crew gone.

name: The Heronry
unique_feature: a dead Oroth tower standing in the wet meadows above Sedgehithe, its top a city of herons' nests
story: The herons have held it as long as anyone has held anything on the Mere. The Tallymen tried to tax the eggs once, and the clerk came back without his hat.
hook: The herons have left all at once, in the middle of the nesting, and flown west.

name: The Fallen Firewatch
unique_feature: a Woodfolk fire-watch tower lying on its side in the bracken where the wind put it
story: The Woodfolk watched the High Wold for fires from it until a winter gale laid it down. They left it lying, because a tower that falls has done its watching.
hook: Somebody has climbed the fallen tower and hung a lantern at its top, which is now its side.

name: The Net Field
unique_feature: a field of eel-nets drying on poles behind Gullhithe, with the net-menders' shelter in the middle
story: Gullhithe mends its nets here in the wind off the fen. The menders can tell a Mere knot from a Sedgish one by feel in the dark, and cut the Sedgish ones out.
hook: A net came back from the water mended with Sedgish knots, by nobody in Gullhithe.

name: The Smoke Coppice
unique_feature: a coppicers' camp in the oak coppice cut for Merrowhithe's smokehouses, the stools older than the Charter
story: Merrowhithe smokes its pike over oak from here and nowhere else, and pays the coppicers in fish, which they say is the only honest wage on the Mere.
hook: One stool has put up a shoot overnight as thick as a man's arm, and the coppicers will not cut it.

name: The Grey Hedge
unique_feature: a Vale farm's hedge gone grey in the White Wood, its hawthorns turned to ash-wood standing in their rows
story: The farm went grey in the Ash Winter and the house is gone. The hedge stands because nobody has told it.
hook: One hawthorn in the grey hedge has come into leaf.

name: The Lambing Fold
unique_feature: a lambing shelter of hurdles on Bram Down, built new each spring on the same ground
story: Rookdown's ewes lamb here out of the wind off the Hush. The shepherds sleep in the fold for the fortnight and swear the down is warmer there than anywhere.
hook: A lamb was born in the fold this spring with a face as grey as ash, and the ewe that bore it belongs to nobody.

name: The Bell Pit
unique_feature: a pit where the dead city's broken bells were buried, their rims showing through the ash
story: The Tolling Order buried every bell it could not hang, so that nobody would ring a broken one. There are two hundred in the pit.
encounter: bell-bearers dig in the pit at night
hook: One of the buried bells has been dug up in the night, hung from a dead tree, and rung once.

name: The Chalk Cell
unique_feature: a hermit's cell cut into the chalk of the Whitecut, with one window looking out over the Mere
story: A hermit lived here for forty years looking at the Spire across the water. The Vale brought her bread, and nobody asked her name.
hook: Bread left at the cell's door is being taken again, after thirty years.

name: The Cockle Beds
unique_feature: the tideflats' cockle-beds staked out in family rows, each stake tied with its family's lantern-knot
story: The reedfolk rake the beds at low water. A stake moved in the night has started more feuds in Sedgemire than eels have.
hook: Every stake on the beds was found moved one row toward the sea.

name: The Last Hearth
unique_feature: the last Hearthstone the Wardens keep on the grey side, its fire banked with chalk
story: The Wardens' patrols turn back here. The fire is kept so that the last thing a patrol sees of the ash is a Vale fire, and the first thing a pilgrim sees of the Vale.
hook: The chalk the fire is banked with has turned grey overnight, right through.

name: The Turned Hut
unique_feature: a shepherd's hut half-buried in drifted ash on the Brow's west slope, its door facing away from the Choir
story: The Brow's shepherds will not graze within sight of the Choir. The last one who did left this hut, and the ash has had it since.
hook: There is fresh straw in the hut, and the ash round the door has been swept.

name: The Larkmouth Bridge
unique_feature: a stone bridge over the Larkbourne's mouth with a bench on it facing the city
story: The Larkbourne's last crossing before the Mere. The Vale's old men walk down on fine evenings to sit on the bench and say what they think of Tollmere, across the water, where it cannot hear.
hook: Somebody sits on the bench every night until dawn, and the old men will only say that he is waiting for the city's lamps to go out.

name: The Weighhouse
unique_feature: the dead city's weighhouse, its great scales fused solid with one pan down
story: The Tallymen have tried for a century to take the scales home. The Order says the pan is down because something was weighed here and found wanting.
hook: The scales have moved: the other pan is down now.

name: The Dale Watch
unique_feature: a Ghast clan watch-house halfway up the dale, a horn hung at its door
story: Ghast keeps a watch on its own dale because of the bridge: whoever comes up is asked which side of the Moot they stand on.
hook: The horn was blown at midnight, and nobody in the watch-house blew it.

name: The Drovers' Bothy
unique_feature: a drovers' bothy of skerr and turf at the bend of Skarldale, with a fire kept in for whoever comes down with the herds
story: The Skarl herds come down the dale in autumn and spend a night here. The bothy is kept by whichever family came down last.
hook: The bothy fire was found lit with a herd's worth of hoofprints round it, going up the dale in spring, when nothing goes up.

name: The Withy Beds
unique_feature: osier-beds cut to stools in rows, where the reedfolk grow the withies for their eel-traps
story: Nauve's Landing weaves every eel-trap in Sedgemire from these withies, and the beds are older than the Landing.
hook: The withies have grown a yard since the new moon, and every one of them has grown toward the Mere.

name: The South Stilts
unique_feature: a reedfolk watch-house on stilts at the delta's southern edge, looking out over the grey
story: Nauvissa raised it in the Ash Winter to see the grey coming. The watchman is paid in eels and has not seen it move in twenty years.
hook: The watchman says the grey has started coming in at night and going back by day, and nobody believes him.

name: The Moot Beacon
unique_feature: the Moot's beacon on the last tor of Rib Edge, lit to tell the lowlands the clans are sitting
story: When the Moot sits at the Rib Cathedral the beacon is lit, and every hold between here and the Mere keeps its quarrels until the Moot rises.
hook: The beacon was lit last night, and the Moot is not sitting.

name: The Chalk Pit
unique_feature: a white pit dug into Bram Down's flank where Rookdown gets its chalk, the diggers' hut at its lip
story: Rookdown cobs its walls with chalk from here and marls its fields with the rest. The pit has been dug so long that the down has a bite out of it you can see from the Hush.
hook: A pick was found standing in the chalk face this spring with a Tallyman's mark on the haft.

name: The Eel Stews
unique_feature: stone-walled ponds in the fen where live eels are kept for the Tollmere market, one pond walled higher than the rest
story: Nauve's Landing sells its eels alive: a dead eel is a Tallyman's price and a live one is a reedfolk's.
hook: The high-walled pond has been found empty with its sluice shut, and its wall is wet on the outside.

name: The Hanging Falls
unique_feature: a waterfall hanging frozen on the Wall's face at the head of Brakh Gill
story: The clans say it thaws one day a year, the day the giants were breathed in, and runs for an hour.
hook: It thawed this spring on the wrong day, and has been running for a week.

name: The Ness Market
unique_feature: a fish market of trestles and awnings on the Stride Ness, the land side of the causeway, where the boats land their catch
story: Lakefolk fishers sell here because a fish sold on the Ness pays no city toll. The Tallymen have been trying to move the toll-line out to the Ness's root for forty years.
hook: The Tallymen have put a clerk at the Ness's tip overnight, with a ledger and no warrant.

name: The Turning Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn of pilgrims' hand-bells on the last bend of the Stair Path, every clapper tied with grey thread
story: A pilgrim who goes down the Stair and comes back up again leaves the bell here, tied silent, and does not say why. The Order counts the bells each spring. The count has never gone down.
hook: One bell on the cairn has been untied, and it has been rung: the thread lies on the stones beside it, cut clean.

name: The Sweeper's Lean-To
unique_feature: a lean-to of pilgrims' staves by the Choir road, a fire, and a broom worn down to the binding
story: Arn Sweeting went down the Stair nineteen years ago, stood a night at the Hushline, and came back up. The Order has no rule for a pilgrim who comes back, so it lets him sweep the grey off the pilgrim road, and he keeps what the broom turns up.
encounter: none; the sweeper at his fire
hook: The broom turned up a hand-bell with a name scratched on it, and the name is not a pilgrim's.

name: The Hayward's Perch
unique_feature: a hayward's lookout on four stilts over the common fields south of Wynstead, a tally of strays cut into every post
story: Merrowby's hayward climbs it at first light to count what has got out of the folds, and cuts the count into the posts. The oldest cuts are at the top, where no hayward alive can reach.
hook: The newest cut on the south post is a notch under and a notch over, and the hayward says he did not cut it.

name: The Novices' Seats
unique_feature: three seats cut in the plateau's lip over the Hush, their backs to the Choir, worn hollow by novices of the Order
story: A novice of the Tolling Order sits here a day and a night before anything else is taught, facing the grey with the Choir behind, and counts the bells without turning round. Those who turn round are sent home, kindly.
hook: One of the seats has been turned in the night to face the Choir, and it is a single stone the size of a cart.

name: Hurdlegate Farm
unique_feature: a lived-in farmstead of whitewashed cob and thatch where the downs road leaves Ashwell, its yard gate made of old sheep-hurdles
story: The Hurdlegates have farmed the foot of the downs since before the Toll fell and keep the drove gate for Ashwell, which means opening it for every flock that comes down and being thanked by none of them.
hook: Somebody has been sleeping in the hay-loft and leaving the eggs they did not eat in a neat row on the sill.

name: Brow End
unique_feature: the last farmstead on the Brow before Rookdown, a long low house of flint with its back to the Hush wind and its byre door painted red
story: Brow End keeps the Brow's cattle through the winter in a byre with a red door, because the Brow's grandmothers said red keeps the grey off a beast, and nobody has lost a cow to the grey since, which proves nothing and settles everything.
hook: The byre door has been painted again overnight, red over red, and the pot is not the farm's.

name: Hatchmoor
unique_feature: a farmstead of chalk-block walls round a square yard on the open downs between the Hare and Hurdle and Bramcombe, its dovecote taller than the house
story: The Hatchmoors breed doves for the Wardens' line, one pair to each beacon, and can tell you which bird flew from which beacon by the ring on its leg and the look in its eye.
hook: A dove came home to the cote this week wearing the ring of a beacon that has not been manned in forty years.

name: Coldharbour
unique_feature: a farmstead in a fold of the downs below Hollin Barrow, its well-house roofed with turf and its walls ringed with the barrow's own fallen stones
story: Coldharbour was built with stones carried off the barrow, before anybody knew better, and every Tollday the farm puts one back on the mound, and the barrow keeps its own count of how many are still owed.
hook: The stone put back last Tollday was back in the farm wall by morning.

name: Pennywort Fields
unique_feature: a miller's farm on the road out of Merrowby to Pennywort's Mill, a thatched house among wheat strips with a quern set by the door for anybody to use
story: The mill's own fields, farmed by the miller's cousins, who grind what they need on the door-quern rather than pay the mill, which is a family argument four generations old.
hook: The door-quern has been turning at night, and in the morning there is cold flour in the trough and no grain gone from the store.

name: Ashway Farm
unique_feature: the southernmost farm in the Vale, on the road from Pilgrim's Ash to Bramcombe, its fields running up to the edge of the grey and ploughed right to it
story: Ashway ploughs to the grey's edge every spring and the grey is a furrow further off by harvest, every year, which the farm takes as its due and the Order takes as a question.
hook: This spring the last furrow was ploughed, and the grey was on the near side of it in the morning.

name: The Last Farm
unique_feature: a farmstead at the Grey End where the downs stop at the Hush, lived in by one old woman who keeps a lamp in the window facing the grey all night
story: Every other house at the Grey End is empty. Maud Rookwell stays because somebody should be the last farm, and keeps the lamp lit so that whatever walks out of the grey at night sees a window before it sees a village.
hook: The lamp was found out one morning and the window open, and Maud says she did not open it.

name: Southgate Farm
unique_feature: a farmstead by the Southgate Stone on the drove to the Brow, with a stone trough in the yard where every drover waters his beasts and pays in gossip
story: Southgate takes no coin for its water, only news, and the farmer's wife has the most complete account of the Vale's comings and goings anybody keeps, written in a hand only her daughters can read.
hook: A drover watered his beasts at the trough last week and paid with news of a village nobody has heard of.

name: Ridgeway Farm
unique_feature: a farmstead on the ridge road where the Vale's fields give out against the Wold's first oaks, half its fences Vale hurdles and half Woodfolk wattle
story: Ridgeway is Vale on the side that faces Tamwick and Woodfolk on the side that faces the Hollow, and the family keeps both customs so thoroughly that it keeps two Long Tables and two naming-days a year.
hook: The oak at the Wold end of the yard has started putting out Vale apple blossom.

name: Fallowgate
unique_feature: a farmstead on the road between Wynstead and Fallowfold whose fields have lain fallow for three years by a vow nobody in the family will explain
story: The Fallowgates made a vow the year the Ninth Waystone's counts stopped, and have not sown since, and live on what the orchard and the bees give them, and are the best-fed family in the Vale.
hook: The fallow field has come up in wheat on its own this spring, in straight drills, as if sown.

name: Larkfield
unique_feature: a farmstead between Wynstead and Merrowby with a lark's nest left undisturbed in the middle of its best field, fenced off with a ring of hurdles
story: The Larkfields found a lark nesting in the wheat the spring the Toll fell, and left it, and a lark has nested in the same spot every spring since, and the ring of hurdles round it has never once been ploughed.
hook: There are two nests in the ring this spring, and the second one is empty and warm.

name: Hazel Bottom
unique_feature: a farmstead in a hazel-hedged bottom under Hollin Barrow on the road to Hazelcombe, with nut-baskets drying on every sill
story: Hazel Bottom sells cob-nuts in Tamwick and hazel rods to the Wold, and its hedges are the oldest in the Vale, laid and re-laid for three hundred years by the same family's hands.
hook: A stretch of hedge has been laid overnight, beautifully, in a style the family's grandmother said died with her grandmother.

name: Cress Mill
unique_feature: an undershot mill wheel in a stone leat off the Cressbourne below Cressbourne, grinding the Vale's barley for the Tamwick brewers
story: The Cress Mill grinds barley for the brewers and nothing else, by an old agreement with the Tallymen that nobody has read in a century, and the miller will not grind a sack of wheat for his own bread.
hook: The wheel has been turning backward at night, against the water, and the barley in the hopper comes out as whole grain.

name: Lark Mill
unique_feature: a timber mill on the Larkbourne below Wynstead, its wheel turning in a leat lined with the Larkbourne's own grey stones
story: Lark Mill grinds for Wynstead and Merrowby both, and its miller keeps the only clock between them, a water-clock off the leat, by which both villages have agreed to be late.
hook: The mill's water-clock has started keeping a different hour from the Toll's, a quarter behind, and the Larkbourne has risen to match it.

name: Skarl Mill
unique_feature: a clan mill of dry-stone and turf on the Skarl Water below Merrowhithe, its wheel paddled with giants' rib-slivers
story: The Skarl Mill grinds oats for three clans, each on its own day, and keeps three hoppers so that no clan's grain touches another's, which is a blood-price matter.
hook: The three hoppers were found mixed one morning, and all three clans are waiting to hear whose fault it was.

name: Rudd Mill
unique_feature: a mill on Rudd Beck below Ruddow, its wheel housed in a long-house of turf so the beck's roar will not wake the hold
story: Clan Rudd built its mill under a turf roof because the Rudds sleep by day in the winter dark and will not have the wheel heard, and the mill grinds only at night.
hook: The mill has been heard grinding at noon, with the wheel chained and the hold asleep.

name: Kharrow Hole
unique_feature: a limestone cave-mouth in the dale side above Kharrow Foot, its lip hung with the clans' blood-price tallies on strings
story: Where a blood-price is too great to pay in coin the clans hang its tally in Kharrow Hole, and the debt is the cave's to keep until somebody comes to pay it, and the strings go back further than the torchlight.
hook: A tally-string at the mouth has been cut down and the debt on it marked paid, and nobody will say who paid it.

name: The Root Hollow
unique_feature: a cave under the roots of a fallen oak in a bank above the ridge road, where the Woodfolk leave a bowl of milk for whatever sleeps inside
story: The Woodfolk say the Root Hollow is where the Lower Wold keeps its bad dreams, and leave milk at its mouth so they stay inside, and nobody has been further in than the milk bowl.
hook: The milk bowl was found full this morning, of something that was not milk, and warm.

name: The Tide Mouth
unique_feature: a sea-cave in the cliff foot west of the Landing, low to the water, where the grey comes in on the tide and goes out again clear
story: The Order says the Tide Mouth breathes the grey: it comes in grey on the flood and goes out clear on the ebb, and somewhere inside the cave keeps what the water leaves.
hook: The tide went out this morning and left a pilgrim's bell on the shell sand, clapper tied, with no name on it.

name: The Carters' Rest
unique_feature: a carters' bench of split oak on a flagged plinth where the charcoal road tips down to Merrowhithe, and a cairn of soot-black stones beside it looking out over the Mere
story: The charcoal carts from the Smoke Coppice stop here to rest the horses before the long drop to the shore. Every carter adds a stone to the cairn with a black thumbprint on it, for luck on the brake.
hook: Every morning this month there has been a white stone on top of the cairn, Vale chalk, and nobody on this road carries chalk.

name: The Charter's End
unique_feature: a squat boundary waystone a pace off the North Road, the Charter's scales cut on its lake face and a clan chain-link on its fell face, the ground worn bare on both sides of it
story: The Charter's writ runs to this stone and blood-price begins beyond it. A Tallymen's bailiff will not serve a writ north of it and a clan will not claim a death south of it, so debtors of both sides have been known to live out their lives within a stride of it.
hook: A debtor has sat against the fell face every night this month, a stride out of the Charter's reach, and the bailiff with his writ sits against the lake face, and they have started sharing a pipe.

name: The Drovers' Trough
unique_feature: a drovers' fire beside a long stone trough where the clan herds are watered before the Narrows, with hurdles stacked for a night pen
story: Every herd driven down the North Road to Tollmere's market is watered here and rested a night before the bridge. The Counting Tower's clerk walks over at dawn to count the beasts for a tax nobody pays, and the drovers give him breakfast for the entertainment.
hook: The trough was found brimming with salt water one morning, and every beast that drank from it that day has refused the Narrows Bridge since.

name: The Forgiving Stones
unique_feature: a heap of lake pebbles round a standing stone in sight of the Counting Tower, each pebble scratched with a sum of money somebody forgave, the newest on top still wet from the shore
story: A ledger has no column for forgiveness, the lakefolk say, so they keep it here. A creditor who lets a debt go carries a pebble up from the shore, scratches the sum on it and adds it to the heap in sight of the Counting Tower, which is the point.
hook: A pebble has been laid scratched with the Counting Tower's own mark and the sum of the North Road tax unpaid since 942, and the tower's clerk swears the Tallymen forgive nothing.

name: The Fair-Day Stone
unique_feature: a milestone on the shore road cut with one notch for every market held at Kharrow Foot, the rows of nicks running down both faces into the grass
story: Lowland carters notch the stone on their way up to every market at Kharrow Foot, so that the clans cannot say a market was missed. The clans keep their own count on a stick at the market's bell-post, and the two counts have never once agreed.
hook: The stone has one notch more than the bell-post's stick, cut fresh, for a market the clans say was never held.

name: The Withy Camp
unique_feature: an eel-trappers' camp on the bank of Rudd Beck, withy traps stacked by the fire and a smoking-rack of split willow
story: Merrowhithe's trappers set their withies in Rudd Beck from the Stair Bridge down to the shore and sleep out beside them, because an eel trap left unwatched on the North Shore is a gift to the next man along.
hook: Every trap on the beck came up full the night the Toll hummed, and the eels in them were the blind white eels from under the Mere, which nobody has ever caught in running water.

name: The Three Rights
unique_feature: three carved stones in a row by the shore road, each cut with its sign: a fish for the right to net, a cup for the right to draw water, a foot for the right to pass
story: Gullhithe and Brindle Mill settled their quarrel over the beck mouth with three stones and three rights, and have argued ever since about which stone is which. Travellers only need the third.
hook: Somebody keeps setting a fourth stone in the verge beside them, uncarved, and every morning Gullhithe has dragged it out and rolled it into the Mere.

name: The Lamp Niche
unique_feature: a waystone with a lamp-niche hollowed in its road face and blackened with soot, facing the ruined beacon on the cliff
story: The niche was cut to hold a lamp for carters feeling their way along the shore road in fog. The smugglers who use the North Cliff Beacon use the niche too: a light in it tells the beacon that the road is clear of the Watch.
hook: The niche was lit last night and the beacon answered it, and every smuggler on the Mere swears the light was not theirs, at either end.

name: Hesper's Boat
unique_feature: a lake-boat dragged far up from the water and left on her side by the road, broken open, her hold made into a shelter with a chest under the standing ribs
story: When the Mere took Hesper Wick's husband she had his boat dragged uphill as far from the water as six Gullhithe men would pull it, and lived in the wreck for thirty years with her back to the lake.
hook: Hesper died at midwinter, and since then somebody has been mending the boat's planking at night, strake by strake, as if she meant to be launched.

name: The Listener's Tent
unique_feature: a Sayers' listening camp by the Stair road, a tent with a writing-board and a line of tuning tines hung in the wind toward the lake
story: The Circle keeps a listener here through the summer to hear the rope on the Pilgrim Stair. A taut rope hums, the Sayers hold, and whatever holds the other end of it hums with it; the listener writes down the note.
hook: The note the rope hums has changed, and the listener packed her tent to carry the news to the Spire herself and left half her papers behind.

name: The Salt Barn
unique_feature: the roofless stone salt-barn at the Narrows where the Salt Isles' salt was stored for the clans, one gable still standing and the floor still white
story: Salt came up the Mere from the Salt Isles traders and was sold to the clans here for curing their mutton. The barn has stood empty since Kharrow Foot started selling salt itself, and its floor has never stopped being white.
hook: The barn floor was found swept, and a line of salt laid across its doorway from post to post, the way the reedfolk lay it against the drowned.

name: The Serpent Watch
unique_feature: a watchers' cairn on the shore bank facing the Mere, a flat stone on its top worn into a seat by forty years of sitting
story: When the serpent was last seen, forty years ago, Gullhithe set a watch on the bank here, and every watcher added a stone at the end of his night. The watch was given up. The cairn was not.
hook: A stone has been added to the cairn every night since the Toll hummed, and each one is wet and weeded, as if it came up out of the Mere.

name: The Unsayers' Stones
unique_feature: three short weathered stones in the verge below Kharrow Gate where travellers who would not say the clans' law back are sent to wait the night
story: The gate-ward tells every traveller the law and asks them to say it back. A traveller who will not is not turned away, only sent down to the stones to sit the night and think, and let up at dawn to try again.
hook: There has been a woman waiting at the stones every dawn this month who will not give a name, and she is gone before the gate-ward comes down.

name: The Pike Shrine
unique_feature: a roadside shrine where Merrowhithe hangs the first smoked pike of the season on a hook over the stone, for whoever is walking hungry
story: Merrowhithe has no opinion about anything, the city says, and it is wrong about one thing: the first fish out of the smoke belongs to the road, and whoever is hungry on it takes the fish and says nothing.
hook: The first pike has been taken three mornings running and a clan bone token left on the hook in its place, a different clan's every morning.

name: The Reeve's Chair
unique_feature: a stone chair by the shore road with a hawthorn grown up through its back, where a reeve sat to hear the shore's disputes before the Charter came
story: Before the Charter the North Shore had a reeve who sat by the road and settled what the fishermen could not. The last reeve died in the chair, and the hawthorn came up through its back the spring after, and nobody has sat to judge since.
hook: Somebody sat in the chair all of last Tollday under the hawthorn and heard disputes, and the whole shore has kept the judgements, and nobody saw their face.

name: The Burner's Clamp
unique_feature: a charcoal-burner's camp by the Skarl Water with a turf-covered kiln smoking beside the road and the burner's lean-to of cut poles
story: The charcoal for Merrowhithe's smokehouses is burned here from the Smoke Coppice's oak. A clamp must smoulder and never flame, so the burner sits up with it for the ten nights it takes, and walks round it every hour, and talks to it.
hook: The clamp has been smouldering for forty days without being fed, and the burner will not open it.

name: Market Brow
unique_feature: a cairn on the brow where the road up from the shore first shows Kharrow Foot's walled market-field below
story: Lowland traders going up to market leave a stone on the cairn and take one away again on the way down. A trader who comes down with no stone to take has lost more at Kharrow Foot than he meant to, and everyone on the road can see it.
hook: Every stone taken down from the cairn after the last market has been brought back up this week and piled at its foot, and every one of them has been split clean in two.

name: The Bier Stone
unique_feature: a flat-topped resting stone on the corpse road from Ruddow to the Rust Scar, a notch cut into its edge for every bier rested on it
story: The Rudd carry their dead from Ruddow to wash their hands in the Rust Scar before they are buried, and the bier is set down here on the way, once, so the dead can look back at the hold. Every rest is notched.
hook: A notch was cut on the stone last week, fresh and deep, and nobody in Ruddow has died.

name: The Wrist Hole
unique_feature: a narrow cave-mouth in the limestone under the Fallen Hand's wrist, blackened by the fires of herders sheltering from the wind
story: The herders say the Wrist Hole goes up inside the giant's arm, and that on a still day you can hear the fingers creak above you. They shelter in its mouth anyway, because it is the only place on that side of the moor out of the wind.
hook: The herders' fire in the Wrist Hole drew backwards last night, the smoke going in, and the dogs would not follow it.

name: The Patter Stone
unique_feature: a waystone on the Low Road scored all over with tinkers' marks, a pot, a chain, a closed hand, telling the next tinker which holds pay and which set dogs on you
story: The tinkers belong to no clan and write to nobody but each other. The stone is their notice-board: a pot for a hold that has work, a closed hand for one that owes, a dog's head for one to walk past quickly.
hook: A new mark has been scored on the stone that no tinker at the camp can read, and they are packing up early because of it.

name: The Brakh's Eye
unique_feature: a giant's skull half sunk in the verge of the Low Road, the road bending round its brow, one eye-socket heaped with the herders' offerings
story: The Oskel say the skull is what was left when the Breath took the giant back and could not take the weight. Herders going by put something in the eye for him to look at, so that he does not look at them.
hook: Something has been sleeping curled in the eye-socket, small as a child, and leaving the offerings untouched.

name: The Oskel Drip
unique_feature: a low cave-mouth in the dale side below Oskelcrag where a spring drips out of the limestone into a worn stone basin
story: Every Oskel child is carried down to the Drip in its first week to drink the first water of its life that has not come through the mine. The clan says it is so the child knows what water tastes like before it learns what the mine does to it.
hook: The spring has started coming out of the rock warm, and humming the same note as the mine's singing shaft.

name: The Singing Seat
unique_feature: a Ghast song-shrine on the dale road, a flat stone for the singer to stand on and the small offerings of the forgiven set round its foot
story: Once a year the Ghast sing the song of forgiveness here, for Kharrow's old shaming at the bridge, whether Kharrow likes it or not. Kharrow does not, which is part of why it is sung.
hook: Somebody from Kharrow came and stood on the singer's stone this year and sang the answer, which nobody in Ghast knew had words.

name: The Two-Clan Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn on the shoulder of Oskel Edge built half of Ghast's dark stone and half of Oskel's pale, where the herders of both dales can see each other's folds
story: Ghast and Oskel herders meet at the cairn to swap strays and news. Each adds a stone of their own dale's colour, so the cairn is a record of who came more often, and each side says it is the other.
hook: The cairn has been rebuilt overnight all of one colour, a grey that is neither dale's, and neither clan will say who did it.

name: The Horn Hole
unique_feature: a slit of a cave in the side of Ghast Dale where the Dale Watch keeps its spare horn and its winter oil against a siege
story: The Ghast keep a second horn in the rock below their watch-house, so that if the watch is ever taken the dale can still be called. Nobody has ever needed it, and it is kept oiled every autumn anyway.
encounter: a scree-hag on the rocks over the mouth after dark
hook: The spare horn was found blown on the night the Dale Watch's horn sounded with nobody in the watch-house, the mouthpiece still wet.

name: The Pitch-Pot Shrine
unique_feature: a tappers' shrine in the Rib Pines, a stone with a clay resin-pot hung over it and the drips of forty summers run down its face in amber
story: The tappers give the first drip of every tree to the stone, so that no chain the pitch goes on rusts in a shameful hour. The stone is so thick with it now that it glows at sunset.
hook: The resin on the stone has come out red this spring, the red of the stand the tappers will not go near, and it is warm to the hand.

name: The Bone-Carvers' Camp
unique_feature: a carvers' camp by the Rib road where splinters of giant bone picked from the beck are laid to dry on a rack beside the fire
story: The Bone Ford sheds splinters in the spring floods, and the carvers camp here to pick them out of Rib Beck and cut the bone tokens every clan-child wears. Each clan has its mark, and a carver who cuts a mark for a clan not his own cuts his thumb first.
hook: The splinters washing down this spring come out of the beck already cut, into tokens with a mark no clan owns, and they keep coming.

name: The Swearers' Rest
unique_feature: a drystone bench on the road up to the Rib Cathedral where oath-takers sit with their sponsors to learn their words, a cairn beside it for each oath kept
story: An oath said wrong inside a giant's bones is said forever, so whoever goes up to swear before the Moot sits here first with a sponsor and learns every word. When the oath has been kept a year the sponsor comes back and adds a stone.
hook: Somebody has cut an oath into the bench's back in careful Skerrish, and it is sworn to no clan.

name: The Beacon Shieling
unique_feature: a beacon-keeper's shieling below the tor, a turf-roofed hut and a drystone fold, with peat stacked by the door for the beacon
story: Whoever keeps the Moot Beacon lives up here through the sitting months with a few sheep and stacks peat for the beacon all summer. The beacon has to catch at the first touch, or the lowlands will not know the clans are sitting.
hook: The peat stack was burned to the ground in the night without the beacon being lit, and the keeper was asleep beside it and woke warm.

name: The Oathbreaker's Stone
unique_feature: a broken waystone on the Moot road, its top lying face-up at its foot where a name was chiselled out of it
story: The name of whoever broke an oath at the Rib Cathedral is cut on the waystone below it, and when the clans decide the breaker is gone from their memory the name is chiselled out and the stone struck through. There have been four in a thousand years.
hook: A name has been cut back into the fallen top overnight, in careful Skerrish, and it is the name of a clan chief now living.

name: The Oath-Takers' Fire
unique_feature: a vigil camp below the Rib Cathedral where oath-takers sit the night before swearing; the fire went out at dawn, the way it must, and the cups are still set round it
story: The one who is to swear keeps vigil here and lets the fire go out at dawn, to show the Moot they come with nothing burning. Crag-wolves come down from the Cathedral's skull on the vigil nights, and nobody is allowed to help.
encounter: crag-wolves down from the Cathedral's skull after dark
hook: The fire was found lit this morning, for the first time in anyone's memory, with nobody due to swear.

name: The Unroofed Hold
unique_feature: the roofless shell of a small hold cut half into the dale side above the Clanless Camp, one gable standing and a bone lintel over its door with the clan name hacked off it
story: A Dreugh family's hold, cast out whole when the father could not pay a blood-price and would not hang its tally in Kharrow Hole. They went to the Clanless. The Dreugh took the roof, as the law says, and left the walls, as the law does not.
encounter: a clanless outrider keeps the shell
hook: Somebody has been living in the shell and paying Dreughow a blood-price in firewood, a bundle a night, left at the hamlet's door.

name: Dreugh's Lookout
unique_feature: a lookout cairn on a spur of Swale Edge where Dreughow keeps an eye on the Clanless Camp below, a flat watcher's stone set on its top
story: Dreughow sends a child up to the cairn every evening to count the fires at the Clanless Camp. More fires than yesterday and the hamlet sleeps with its door barred; fewer, and somebody from Dreughow goes down in the morning to find out who has gone.
hook: The watcher's stone on top of the cairn has been turned in the night to face Dreughow, not the camp.

name: The Shaft Pebbles
unique_feature: a cairn of river pebbles round a stone on the Oskel's bank, each pebble for an Oskel miner who went down the shaft and did not come up
story: Where the river leaves Oskeld Dale is as far from the shaft as the clan's memory will carry a miner. Every pebble on the cairn is a name, and on the one night a year the mine does not sing the Oskel come down and say every one.
hook: A pebble has been laid for Brenn ko-Oskel, who is still at work underground and sends up word by every shift that he is well.

name: The Cart-Wards' Post
unique_feature: a clan cart-wards' post on the Low Road, a fire and a lean-to where Brindle's warriors wait to walk the ore-carts past the Clanless Camp, their shields stacked by the fire
story: The Clanless take from Brindlecrag's ore-carts and call it blood-price, so every cart that goes by the overhang goes with Brindle warriors walking beside it. The wards wait here between carts and keep the fire in.
hook: The Clanless have stopped taking from the carts, all at once, and the wards cannot find out why, and would very much like to.

name: Brindle's Luck
unique_feature: a stone by the pine road that every Brindle ore-carter rubs with pitch-oil in passing, till it shines like a chestnut
story: The road from Brindlecrag down past the Three Sisters is the steepest the ore-carts take, and a carter who does not oil the stone on the way down does not trust his brake on the way down either, which comes to the same thing.
hook: The stone was scraped dull overnight and a clanless man's loosened chain-link left lying on top of it.

name: The Gorge Porters
unique_feature: a porters' camp in the bottom of Kharrow Gorge where loads are shifted off lowland carts onto clan mules for the climb to the Hold
story: No lowland cart goes up Kharrow Gorge on the clans' say. Loads are carried from here to the Hold on mules, by Kharrow porters, at Kharrow rates, and a load that cannot be split between two mules does not go up at all.
hook: A load was left at the camp addressed to Kharrow Hold in a Tallyman's hand, too heavy for two mules, and it hums whenever the Hold's bell rings.

name: The Link-Keeper's Fire
unique_feature: the link-keeper's fire at the end of the Chain Bridge, the bridge's loosened links hung ringing on a line between two posts in the wind off the gorge
story: When a clan is shamed, one link of its chain on the bridge is struck off and the bridge leans. The link-keeper hangs every struck link here until the shame is paid and the link goes back, and can tell each clan's link by its ring.
hook: Ghast's link went back onto the bridge last night, and the link-keeper did not put it there.

name: The Brother's Seat
unique_feature: a drystone bench on the Low Road with a cairn beside it, looking up to the middle ledge of the Three Sisters where their Hearthstone stands behind the water
story: The Rudd sisters carried the Hearthstone up so that their exiled brother would be remembered somewhere warm. He was not allowed nearer to it than the road, so he built this seat where he could see it, and sat in it until he died.
hook: A clanless man sits in the seat every dusk and weeps, and will not say for whom, and the Rudd have started leaving him bread.

name: The Burned Ore-House
unique_feature: the roofless stone ore-house on the Low Road where Brindlecrag's carts once overnighted, its door burned out and one gable black to the top
story: The Clanless burned the ore-house the first winter they came to the overhang, and called it the blood-price for a Brindle debt none of them would name. The carts have not stopped here since.
encounter: two clanless outriders on the road by day
hook: New-cut roof beams have been hauled up and set across the walls, and nobody in Brindlecrag or at the overhang will say who is building.

name: The Last Cairn
unique_feature: a snow-capped cairn at the head of the Windgate Cleft, the last thing a traveller passes on the way to the pass
story: Travellers going north over the Windgate take a stone from the cairn and put one back if they return. The cairn is the count of those who came back, and it has been shrinking for as long as the gate-warden's family has kept the Watch.
hook: The cairn has been growing all winter, a stone a night, though nobody has crossed the pass in years.

name: The Ice-Cutters' Camp
unique_feature: an ice-cutters' camp on the snow slope below Frostmother's Cradle, the fire went out long ago, saws and sledges still standing in the drift
story: Kharrow Hold cuts its summer ice from the slope below the Cradle, because the ice there does not melt on the way down. The cutters camp for a week each winter and do not go nearer the Cradle than the camp.
hook: The ice they cut last winter has not thawed in the Hold's cellars in a whole summer, and each block has a shape frozen in it that was not there when it was cut.

name: The Knotted Rope
unique_feature: a rope-shrine by the Low Road, a stone with a hole through it and a knotted rope tied through the hole, every knot a name somebody wanted kept
story: The clans say memory is a hand on the rope, and this is the rope. A traveller who is afraid a name will be forgotten ties a knot for it and says the name once, and the Brindle who keep the shrine say it again every morning.
hook: A knot has been untied from the middle of the rope, and the name that was in it is gone from every Brindle's memory but one child's.

name: The Shift Stone
unique_feature: a waystone halfway up the Oskeld mine road, a notch cut into it for every shift that went up and a cross for every shift that did not come down
story: Every shift going up to Oskeld Mine cuts its notch on the way past, and the overseer checks the notches against the shifts coming down. The crosses are few and old, and every Oskel child can say where each one is.
hook: Last week a shift's notch was cut that the overseer did not send up the mine road, and the mine sang all that night.

name: Gann's Shieling
unique_feature: an Oskel goatherd's shieling on the dale floor below the Deadground, a turf-roofed hut and a drystone fold with every beast in it tied by a rope
story: The Oskel stopped grazing the dale below the mine when the goats began walking into the shaft. Old Gann ko-Oskel was the last to leave. This spring he has come back with a new flock, and ties every beast in the fold on its own rope.
hook: Every morning the ropes in the fold are found untied and neatly coiled, and every beast is still there, standing facing the mine.

name: The Debtors' Lean
unique_feature: three leaning stones on the Ruddow road below Kharrow Hole, where those whose tallies hang in the cave stop to lean with their backs to it
story: A debtor whose blood-price is too great to pay has its tally hung in Kharrow Hole, and must not look at the cave while passing it. They stop at the stones, lean with their backs to the Hole, get their breath, and go on facing the road.
hook: A debtor was found asleep against the middle stone, facing the Hole, and his tally in the cave has been cut down and marked paid.

name: The Neither Stone
unique_feature: a boundary waystone in Skarldale's summer grass marking the Moot's line, the Skarl mark and the Rudd mark both chiselled off it so that it belongs to nobody
story: The Skarl and the Rudd fought sixty years over this grass, and the Moot ended it by giving it to neither. The stone was set to mark the grass that is nobody's, and both clans' marks were cut off it the same day, by both clans, in front of the Moot.
hook: Both marks have been cut back onto the stone overnight, side by side, in the same hand.

name: The Skarl Skull
unique_feature: a giant's skull lying in the dale's grass beside the track below the Black Keep, its eye-sockets used as a byre for heifers
story: The Skarl say the skull is their giant's and the Rudd say it is theirs. The Moot gave it, like the grass, to neither, and the heifers of both have sheltered in its eye-sockets in bad weather since, which the Moot says was the point.
hook: The heifers will not go into the sockets any more, and something has been cropping the grass inside them short.

name: The Smelters' Stone
unique_feature: a smelters' shrine under the pines below the Smeltings, a stone where the first ingot of every smelt is laid and left for a night
story: Iron from the top of the vein, lead from the middle and silver from the bottom, the Brindle say, and the first ingot of each goes to the stone for a night, so the fell knows the clan did not take more than it gave back.
hook: The ingot laid last month was taken in the night, and a lead one left in its place, cast in the shape of a hand.

name: The Namers' Fire
unique_feature: the fire where Kharrow youths wait out the night before crossing Kharrow Force's lip, a ring of stones and one stool for the one who waits
story: A Kharrow youth crosses the lip of the Force on the iron rope on their naming day, and waits here the night before, alone, with whoever of the clan will come and sit outside the firelight and say nothing.
hook: A youth waited here all night last week and crossed the lip at dawn, and no clan will own her.

name: The Newsmonger's Stone
unique_feature: a waystone by the Drove Chain chalked all over with the news paid at the chain, washed off by every rain and chalked again
story: The Drove Chain is lifted for a beast from every herd and a piece of news from every traveller. The chain-ward chalks each piece on the stone so the next traveller can read it for nothing, which the Ghast think is theft and the Brindle think is funny.
hook: The news chalked on the stone yesterday is next week's, in the chain-ward's own hand, and he says he did not write it.

name: The Old Toll-House
unique_feature: the roofless first toll-house of the Windgate, abandoned when the snow came down the pass, one gable standing out of the drift
story: The Windgate's toll was taken here before the snow came lower every winter and the warden's family moved down to the Watch of the Gate. A toll-house where nobody comes to pay is only a house, and the snow took the roof.
hook: Somebody has paid the toll here, at the old house, in coin struck before the Chain Years.

name: The Slag Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn of glassy black slag from the Smeltings on the shoulder of the Brindlecrag road, each lump the size of a fist
story: Every Brindle smelter throws the first lump of slag from their first smelt onto the cairn, so there is a lump there for every smelter the clan has had. The children can name the oldest by their colour.
hook: A lump of slag has been found on the cairn with a silver ring grown up out of the glass, and when it is struck it hums a note the smiths refuse to name.

name: The Listening Stones
unique_feature: three leaning stones bored through on the Oskeld mine road, where the singing of the shaft comes out of the rock
story: Oskel miners put their ear to the holes in the stones before going down, to hear whether the shaft is singing true. A shaft that sings true is a shaft that holds; a shaft singing flat is one to stay out of.
encounter: a stone-thrall stands among the stones after midnight
hook: The stones have started singing on their own when the shaft is quiet, one verse behind it.

name: The Laid Fire
unique_feature: a Woodfolk way-shelter where the charcoal road enters the oaks, a bark-roofed lean-to over a ring of stones with a fire kept laid in it for whoever comes
story: Leave is not asked in the Wold, and shelter is simply there. At every road's edge the Woodfolk keep a fire laid and never lit. A traveller may light it, and before leaving must lay it again as well as they found it, which is the only toll the Wold takes.
hook: The fire has been found lit at every dawn this month, and laid again better than the Woodfolk lay it, with wood from no tree that grows in the Wold.

name: The Masons' Lodge
unique_feature: the roofless lodge where the Builders' quarrymen slept below the Old Quarry, one gable standing and the Oroth masons' marks cut in its door-jamb
story: The stone for the Long Stride came out of the Old Quarry, and the quarrymen slept here. Their marks on the jamb are the marks on the causeway's stones, which Tollmere would rather not hear, and every Sayer who comes to look copies them.
hook: New marks have been cut in the jamb, fresh and sharp, and they are the marks on the half-cut block still hanging in the quarry face.

name: The Leave Stone
unique_feature: a waystone at the Wold end of the Skarl Bridge road with a bow-knot cut in its face, where travellers out of clan country stop and ask the Wold's leave aloud
story: The Woodfolk give no leave and refuse none; asking is the custom, not the answer. Clan folk coming over the Skarl Bridge stop at the stone and ask aloud anyway, because in their country a host is asked, and nobody answers, which is the Wold's way of saying yes.
hook: Something answered this week, a voice out of the oaks, and it said no.

name: The Torch Stone
unique_feature: a stone by the Ormhold road above the Blackgill's falls, with a basket of pitch torches kept beside it for throwing down into the gill
story: Weavers breed in the Blackgill's dark, and the Northwold's woodfolk throw a lit torch down each fall before they pass. The basket by the stone is kept full by whoever passes with a torch to spare, and nobody passes without taking three.
encounter: a weaver drops on travellers after dark
hook: The basket has been emptied every night and no torches have gone down the falls; they have been found deep in the gill, standing upright in a ring, still burning.

name: The Silk-Gatherers' Camp
unique_feature: a camp at the lip of the Blackgill where woodfolk gather weaver silk from the oaks at noon, long poles and reels stacked beside the fire
story: Weaver silk is worth its weight in brass in Tollmere and is gathered only at noon, when the weavers sleep, by woodfolk who wind it off the oaks on long poles and do not stay in the gill a moment past the first shadow.
hook: The silk gathered this week comes off the oaks already spun, into a thread finer than any spinner in Tollmere can make, and knotted every hand's length in the same pattern.

name: The Two Countries Bench
unique_feature: a bench of split oak on a flagged plinth at the Skarl road's last rise in the Wold, a cairn of granite beside it, looking north over the Skarl Water into clan country
story: Northwold foresters sit here in the evening and watch the clan fires come out on the fells. The custom is to sit facing north, with the Wold at your back, so the Wold knows you are keeping watch for it and not on it.
hook: Someone has turned the bench round to face the Wold, and the foresters who sat on it that way say they heard the wood holding its breath.

name: The Uncarried
unique_feature: three rough-cut granite blocks the Builders quarried and never carried, standing on end by the road below the Old Quarry
story: The Builders cut more stone for the Long Stride than they laid. Three blocks were left at the roadside, stood on end so they would not be buried, and the Woodfolk have let them stand, because a thing left waiting for somebody is not the Wold's to move.
hook: One of the blocks has moved a stride nearer the Mere overnight, and there are no drag-marks in the moss.

name: The Planters' Camp
unique_feature: a planters' camp at the forest crossing, oak and ash saplings heeled into a trench beside the fire, waiting for the notches on the Tally Hearth's sticks
story: A tree taken is a notch cut, and a notch cut is a tree planted by the next spring: the Wold's one law that is written down. The planters camp here each spring with the saplings and go out with the sticks from the Tally Hearth, one tree for every notch.
hook: Every sapling heeled in at the camp has been planted overnight in a single line running east toward the Briar, and they are taller than a man already.

name: The Moss Bed
unique_feature: a tender's shrine on the road to Mossgrave, a flat stone under a roof of bark where the moss for new graves is started and kept damp
story: The Woodfolk bury under moss, not stone, and a new grave's moss is started here, by the road, where everyone passing sees it growing and knows somebody has died. When it has taken it is carried to Mossgrave and laid over them.
hook: A new moss has come up on the bed that nobody started, and the tenders say it has already been given a name, and not one of them knows it.

name: The Mourners' Fire
unique_feature: a Hart-Knight's vigil fire by the road below the Knight's Mound, a tent and a cleared ring with antlers hung on the oaks round it
story: The Hart-Knights keep the Wold's last knight in their memory, and one of them keeps a watch-fire here through the dark months. The Woodfolk call them mourners who have forgotten what for, and leave them alone, which the knights take as respect.
encounter: a Hart-Knight keeps the fire after dark
hook: The knight at the fire has been seen leaving a cup of water on the Mound at midwinter, which is the Woodfolk's custom, and which no knight has ever done.

name: The Fourth Brother
unique_feature: a lone grey stone by the road like an old man in a cloak, walking away from the Grey Man's tor
story: The Grey Man is three brothers who stood still to listen to the Standing Moot's hum and forgot to stop. The Woodfolk say there was a fourth, who remembered to stop, and has been walking home ever since, a stride a century.
hook: The Fourth Brother has moved three strides down the road since spring, and has turned his head.

name: The Firewatchers' Camp
unique_feature: the camp the High Wold's firewatchers kept after their tower fell; the fire went out when they left, and the cups are still set round it
story: When the gale laid the Fallen Firewatch down, its watchers camped here and kept the watch from the ground for a season, until the Wold agreed that a fallen tower had done its watching. They let the fire go out and walked home.
hook: Somebody has been sleeping in the cold camp and watching the east, and has chalked a count of fires on its stones: fires in the High Wold where nobody is to light them.

name: The Briar Root
unique_feature: a root-cave under a root of the Briar as thick as a man, come up through the High Wold two miles from the wall
story: The Briar's roots go under the whole Wold, and where one breaks the surface the Woodfolk leave it and mark the place. This one arches out of the ground like a doorway, and the dark under it goes further back than the root should.
encounter: thornhounds round the mouth after dark
hook: The root has put out a green shoot, the first green on any root of the Briar in living memory, and thornhounds lie round the mouth as if they were keeping it.

name: The Road Knot
unique_feature: a lamp-shrine on the Fernhold lane where the Hollow's knot-keepers light a lamp for travellers, set in a stone under a hood of bark
story: Every knot lit in the Grandfather is lit from the one before it, back to the coal the women carried in. The lamp here is lit from the Knot-Hearth each dusk, so that the road to Fernhold carries the Hollow's own fire as far as the stone.
hook: The lamp has been found lit from a fire that is not the Knot-Hearth's, and its flame burns blue.

name: The Silence Stones
unique_feature: three stones by the Fernhold lane below Wold Force where those who lost at the bench go to say what they did not say there
story: Fernhold settles its arguments at Wold Force: whoever sits longest on the bench in the spray without speaking wins. The loser may say everything they held back, but only here, to the stones, out of the winner's hearing.
hook: Somebody has been talking to the stones every night for a month, a long quarrel, and in the mornings the stones are wet with spray though the falls are two hundred paces away.

name: The Antler-Smith's House
unique_feature: the roofless house of the antler-smith who made the Hart-Knights' helms, one gable standing and the cold forge still in its corner
story: The last smith who could set a hart's antlers into a helm lived here under the Hart Bones and died without an apprentice. The knights wear their helms until they break now, and bury them with their owners, and there are fewer every year.
hook: Smoke rises from the cold forge at night, and in the morning there is a new helm on the anvil, antlered, and sized for a child.

name: The Poachers' Cache
unique_feature: a poachers' fire in a hollow off the Moot road, hart hides pegged out to dry and antlers bundled for the carts to Tollmere
story: The poachers take hart in the Greatwood and sell the antlers in Tollmere as Oroth relics. The Woodfolk have said nothing, which is the custom, and the Hart-Knights have said a great deal, which has not helped.
encounter: two poachers at the fire after dark
hook: The antlers bundled for Tollmere were found unbundled in the morning and hung in the oaks round the fire, the way the Hart-Knights hang theirs in the Antler Chapel.

name: Wenna's House
unique_feature: the roofless chalk-cob house of a Vale woman who married into the Wold, one gable standing, her grave inside its walls under a stone lid and a Woodfolk moss
story: Wenna Tamwood came from Tamwick and married a forester, and wanted to be buried both ways: under a Vale stone, so she would be remembered, and under a Woodfolk moss, so she would be let go. Her family did both, and the house fell in round her.
hook: The moss on her grave has been let go, as the Woodfolk do when nobody remembers the name, and somebody has cut her name into the lid in Vale letters.

name: The Oil-Carriers' Stone
unique_feature: a flat stone on the Moot road where the oil jars are set down to rest, rubbed with forty years of spilled oil until it shines like a chestnut
story: The Standing Moot's stones are oiled by hand every week, and the oil is carried up from Fernhold in jars on a yoke. The carriers rest the jars here, and what spills is left on the stone, because oil that falls on the road to the Moot is already the Moot's.
hook: The oil jars left here to rest overnight were found empty in the morning and every stone of the Moot oiled, by nobody who had carried the jars.

name: The Hart Count
unique_feature: a waystone on the Moot road cut with a hart's head, notched down both faces by the verderer for every hart counted in the Greatwood
story: The verderer walks the Moot road every autumn and counts the harts, and notches the stone, and the count is the Wold's wealth as far as the Woodfolk keep any. The notches have been fewer every year since the poachers came.
hook: The notches have begun to be filled in, one by one, with pitch, as if harts that were counted are being uncounted.

name: The Drunk Stones
unique_feature: three leaning stones at the bend of the Wold Road where Tamwick's cider carts slow for the corner
story: Tamwick's carts take the Wold Road to the Hollow with the cider, and slow for the bend here, and slop. The carters say the stones lean because they have been drinking what spills for three hundred years, and every carter tips a cup at the bend to keep them from falling over entirely.
hook: The stones stood straight one morning, upright as the day they were set, and had leaned again by noon.

name: The Bread Stone
unique_feature: a stone at the Hollow road's bend where Tamwick's carters leave a loaf for the children of Grandfather Hollow
story: The Hollow buys Tamwick's cider and will not take it without a gift going back, which is custom. So the carters leave a loaf on the stone, and the Hollow's children run down the road to meet the carts and take it, and the carts are welcomed in.
hook: The loaf has lain untaken on the stone for a week, and the Hollow's children say they were told not to come to the road, and will not say by whom.

name: The Burnt Lodge
unique_feature: the roofless lodge of a woodfolk family who cut timber within bowshot of the Sentinels, its walls scorched black and one gable standing
story: The Woodfolk do not cut within bowshot of the clearing where the wardens gather. One family did, for a lodge, and the wardens came through the wood at dusk and stood round it all night, and in the morning it was burning and the family was on the road to Tamwick.
encounter: a warden stands in the lodge at dusk, and minds its own business
hook: A warden has been seen standing inside the burnt lodge at dusk, alone, with its back to the Sentinels.

name: The Foxfire-Pickers' Camp
unique_feature: a pickers' camp above the Foxgill ravine where foxfire fungus dries on bark trays beside the fire, glowing faintly after dark
story: Foxfire fungus is worth a month's charcoal to Tollmere's alchemists, and it grows only on the ravine walls under Foxfire Falls. The pickers go down on ropes by day and dry it by the fire at night, when the trays glow like a village seen from a hill.
hook: The pickers have stopped going down the ravine: the fungus on the walls has started to glow in the shape of hands.

name: The Flood Stone
unique_feature: a waystone by the Wold Water road cut with the height of every flood since the Wold was settled, the oldest mark high above a man's head
story: The rafters cut a line on the stone at the height of every flood, and the year beside it, so that a rafter who wants to know how bad a spring can be only has to look up. The oldest line is higher than anyone has seen the Wold Water, and nobody knows who cut it.
hook: A new flood mark has been cut above all the others, the highest on the stone, and the year beside it is next spring's.

name: The Coppice Round
unique_feature: a coppicers' camp in a clearing of hazel stools, hurdles and bundles of rods stacked by the fire for the carts to Tamwick
story: Hazelwick cuts its hazel on a seven-year round, a different stand each winter, and every stool has a name and a family. This is the year's cutting-camp, and the families who are not on speaking terms camp at opposite ends of it.
hook: The stools cut last winter have grown seven years' rods in one spring, and Hazelwick cannot agree whose turn it now is.

name: The Rafters' Locker
unique_feature: a root-cave in the Wold Water's bank under an old alder, where the rafters keep their spare poles and ropes out of the rain
story: The rafters make up their rafts behind the Log Boom and keep their spare gear in the hole under the alder, where it stays dry. Nobody locks it. Leave is not asked in the Wold, and the rafters have never lost a pole.
hook: The spare poles have been taken out every night and put back wet, and the ropes have been knotted into a raft's lashings for a raft nobody has built.

name: The Wall-Watchers' Fire
unique_feature: a forester's watch-fire at the foot of the Thornmarch track, a bark lean-to and a fire kept in all night facing the Briar
story: Since the grey patches began to spread in the Briar, Fernhold keeps somebody at the wall's foot through the night, with a fire, facing it. Nobody has said what the watcher is to do if the grey comes down, and nobody has asked.
encounter: ash-wights wander up from the Breach after dark
hook: The watcher woke at dawn to find the grey patch nearest the fire gone green again, and the fire let out, and ash tracked from the Breach to the cold hearth and back.

name: The Cider Shrine
unique_feature: a Vale hedge-shrine in the last field before the oaks, where Tamwick folk going into the Wold leave a cup of cider on the stone
story: The Wold gives no leave and asks none, which makes Vale folk uneasy, so Tamwick thanks it in advance instead: a cup of cider on the stone at the edge of the last field, left full, and found empty coming home.
hook: The cup has been left full a fortnight, and the Tamwick carters say the Wold has stopped drinking with them.

name: The Sawyers' Bench
unique_feature: a bench of split oak on a flagged plinth where the ridge road looks out over the Vale, the Sawpit brothers' noon seat, a cairn of sawn-off knots at one end
story: The two brothers at the Sawpit have not spoken in eleven years and eat their noon bread here at opposite ends of the bench, looking at the Vale, with their backs to each other's half. Each adds a knot from the day's planks to the cairn.
hook: One of the brothers has been seen eating his noon bread in the middle of the bench.

name: The Last Dry Mile
unique_feature: a milestone on the Westway where the downs' chalk gives out and the reedfolk's boardwalk begins, cut with the miles to Merrowby on one face and a lantern on the other
story: Vale carters and reedfolk meet at the stone and swap loads, because no Vale carter will take a wheel onto the boardwalk and no reedfolk will pull a cart. The lantern face is the reedfolk's: past it, carry a light.
hook: The lantern cut on the stone's face has been blacked in with soot overnight, which is the reedfolk's sign for a drowned person's lantern.

name: The Lantern-Wright's Camp
unique_feature: a reedfolk lantern-maker's camp on a peat hummock beside the Westway, horn panes drying on a rack by the fire
story: Every lantern hung on the Boardwalk Gate and every lantern sunk with the reedfolk's dead is made here, from horn scraped thin enough to read through. The lantern-wright sings rounds while she works, alone, taking every part herself.
hook: Every lantern made here this month has come out with its flame burning downward, toward the water.

name: The Lead-Carriers' Rest
unique_feature: a lead-carriers' stopping place at the edge of the fen below Oskel Ford, pack frames stacked beside the fire and a lantern pole marking the dry path
story: Oskel miners carry their lead down out of the dale to trade at Isseva, and rest here before the fen. The reedfolk never cross the ford the other way, and the miners never ask them to; the rest is the one place both stand.
hook: The reedfolk have started leaving a lantern lit on the pole for the Oskel carriers, which the reedfolk do for nobody who is not drowned.

name: The Drowned Byre
unique_feature: the roofless stone byre of a farm the fen came up over, one gable standing out of the reeds of the Carr
story: There was dry pasture on this edge of the fen before the Mere fell and the delta spread, and a clan family kept cattle here, the only clan folk who ever farmed on the flat. The fen came up a hand a year until the byre stood in it, and they drove the beasts up the dale and never came back down.
encounter: bog-drowned climb out of the Carr after dark
hook: Cattle have been heard lowing in the byre at night, and in the morning there is fresh dung on a floor the water has covered for forty years.

name: The Long Table Bench
unique_feature: a bench of chalk blocks on a flagged plinth on the downs road, a cairn of flints beside it, looking north down the Vale to the Mere
story: Walkers going up to the Hare and Hurdle sit here for the view of the whole Vale laid out to the water. Each Long Table the inn's people carry a flint up from the feast and add it to the cairn, one for every harvest the downs have kept.
hook: Somebody has been leaving a place laid on the bench, a plate, a cup and a slice of pie, as if for a guest at the Long Table who has not come.

name: Ribbon Meg's Fire
unique_feature: a pedlar's camp on the Brow road, a painted cart and a fire, ribbons for sale hung on a line between two stakes
story: Ribbon Meg has worked the Brow's farms for thirty years with ribbon, thread, pins and gossip, and camps at this bend because it is a day's walk from Bramcombe and a day's walk from Rookdown, and she does not like either of them enough to sleep there.
hook: Meg has sold nothing but candles this month, one to every farm on the Brow, and every farm has set its candle in the window that faces south.

name: The Hound's Bowl
unique_feature: a hedge-shrine below the Chalk Hound where the Vale leaves a bowl of water for the hill figure on hot days
story: The Chalk Hound is scoured every seven years by everyone who can hold a rake, and in the years between the Vale leaves him water when the weather is hot, because a dog cut into a hill is still a dog and should not be thirsty.
hook: The bowl has been drunk dry every morning of this hot spell, and there are chalk paw-prints on the stone, each the size of a cartwheel.

name: The Millers' Stone
unique_feature: a broken milestone on the mill road, its top lying face-up at its foot with 'Pennywort's Mill, 1 mile' still on it
story: The cart carrying the mill's first stone up from the quarry broke this milestone when the millstone slid off it, which was the first bad luck, and the stone cracked on its first turn, which was the second. The milestone was left broken, to keep count.
hook: The broken top has been set back on its stump overnight, and the mile cut on it now reads nothing at all.

name: Gorse Hut
unique_feature: a shepherd's summer hut of flint and turf under the gorse on the Brow, with a drystone fold for the ewes beside it
story: Rookdown's shepherds summer their ewes on this corner of the Brow and sleep in the hut in turns. It is the last roof before the Thornmarch's gorse, and the warrener from the camp below used to come up for his supper.
hook: The warrener who went missing at the Long Table has been sleeping in the hut, the shepherd says, and will not come out, and asks only for rabbit.

name: The Boys' Lookout
unique_feature: a bandits' lookout fire at the edge of Rook Wood where the Larkbourne Boys' eastern gang watch the Brow road, a stolen boundary-bell hung over it
story: The Larkbourne Boys' eastern gang keep a lookout here for the Hanging Coombe, a fire and a sentry, with a view of the Brow road from Bramcombe to Rookdown. Travellers who see the fire go round by the fields.
encounter: two bandits keep the lookout after dark
hook: The lookouts have started ringing their stolen boundary-bell whenever anybody comes up the road, and they say it is a warning to the travellers, not to the gang.

name: The Dodgers' Stone
unique_feature: a waystone at the Lake Road's fork where carters turn off to go round the Stride's Foot weighbridge, a cart-wheel scratched on it and a finger pointing the back way
story: Everything that goes to Tollmere on wheels is weighed and priced at Stride's Foot, unless it goes round by the shore, which is slower, muddier and free. The finger was scratched by a carter long ago. The Tallymen have had it chiselled off four times.
hook: Somebody has chiselled the pointing finger round to face the weighbridge, and the Tallymen swear it was not them.

name: The Laundry Punt
unique_feature: a laundresses' punt dragged up the bank of the Lake Road and left on her side, broken open, a line of washing-pegs still along her rail
story: Before the Stride's Foot road was mended, Tollmere's washing came across the water in this punt twice a week for the Wash-Stones. When the laundresses started walking over the causeway the punt was dragged up the bank and left, and nobody has the heart to burn it.
hook: The punt has been found full of wet washing every morning, beautifully folded, shirts and shifts that nobody in Tollmere owns.

name: The Rafters' Knots
unique_feature: a shrine on the east shore road where the rafters leave a knot of rope on the stone for every raft that reached the city whole
story: A raft of Wold timber poled across the Mere to Tollmere's timber quay comes whole or comes in pieces, and the rafters give the Mere a knot for every one that came whole. The stone is furred with rope ends like an old dog.
hook: A knot has been left on the stone for a raft that nobody at the camp launched.

name: The Salvagers' Fire
unique_feature: a salvagers' fire on the east shore where the Mere's driftwood is sorted, good timber stacked to one side and the rest burned
story: The Mere gives up timber from every broken raft and every beached barge, and the salvagers sort it on the shore: good oak for Tollmere's yards, the rest for the fire. Nobody salvages from the Beached Barge; the timber there is argued over.
hook: The salvagers found a barge's name-board in the drift, freshly painted, with the Beached Barge's name on it.

name: The Old Shore Bench
unique_feature: a bench on a flagged plinth on the old shore road where the Mere once lapped, a cairn of lime-white stones beside it, looking over the water at Tollmere
story: The Mere has fallen ten metres since the Toll came down, and left its beaches up the hill like steps. The old folk of Stride's Foot sit on the bench where their grandparents paddled and say the water is resting, whatever the Sayers say.
hook: The water has been seen at the bench's feet at dawn, lapping where it has not lapped for forty years, and gone again by breakfast.

name: The Weight Stone
unique_feature: a waystone by the lime road with a hollow cut in its top where the burners weigh a sample basket of lime against the Tallymen's iron
story: The lime-burners are paid by weight, which everybody agrees is fair, and the weight is taken here on the road where both sides can watch, with the Tallymen's own iron in the stone's hollow and the burners' own basket beside it.
hook: The Tallymen's iron has been found in the hollow three mornings running, and each morning it weighs a pound less.

name: The Hum Cairn
unique_feature: a lone cairn on the east shore road with a brass tuning fork bedded in its top stone, set by the Listening Post's clerk
story: The clerk at the Listening Post cannot sing, and so cannot hold the Toll's note in his head between nights. He bedded a fork in the cairn tuned to the hum, and strikes it on his way to work to know what he is listening for.
hook: The fork has been humming on its own at night, the Toll's note, a quarter-tone sharp.

name: The Wardens' Halt
unique_feature: a Warden patrol's halting-place on the Bramcombe road below Hound Watch, a fire and a lean-to and the pole where the patrol hangs its hand-bell while it rests
story: The Wardens' patrols out of Hound Watch rest here on their way down the Vale. Down-wolves come up out of Lamb's Bottom after dark, so the halt is never left without a fire, and the patrol's bell is hung on the pole to be rung if the fire has to be left.
encounter: down-wolves come up out of Lamb's Bottom after dark
hook: A patrol came down and found another patrol's fire already lit at the halt and its bell on the pole, and nobody from the Rest was out that night.

name: The Grey-Wind Cairn
